title: Gimlé Requirements Matrix
preamble:
This matrix was reverse-engineered directly from the Gimlé codebase as it stood at commit `919bd4063ab8ef5a430e1e3ed8bf2f12ddacd640` (2026-08-17), on branch `claude/gimle-requirements-matrix-lfkqqe`. Every entry below is grounded in code and test source actually read in the repository — main sources, `module-info.java` files, test classes, Gherkin `.feature` files, and (for the web console family) frontend routes/stores/repositories — not in the project's own planning docs (`gimle-PROJECT-v2.md`, `CLAUDE.md`) or aspirational design intent. Where behavior is stubbed, deliberately deferred, or documented as an accepted v1 limitation, the entry is marked `Partial` in the Status column with the reason inline; nothing here describes intended-but-unimplemented behavior.

**Scope**: all 27 Maven modules in the reactor — 564 distinct requirements identified, grouped by module below. IDs are sequential (`GIMLE-001`…`GIMLE-564`) in module order; they are stable identifiers for this document only, not references to any other tracker.

**Method note on Test Coverage classification**: `Yes` means the entry cites one or more real test class/method names; `Partial` means no dedicated test exists but the behavior is exercised indirectly (through another module's integration test, a smoke test, or a Holmgang scenario); `None` means no test — direct or indirect — was found for that specific behavior.

requirements.feature: Semantic module versioning
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator, I want module versions parsed and compared per a strict major.minor.patch[-qualifier] grammar.
gherkinSteps: Given "1.2.3-rc1" parsed via Version.parse, When compared against unqualified "1.2.3", Then the unqualified version compares as greater.

requirements.feature: Version range constraint matching
requirements.userStory: As a module author, I want to declare a dependency's acceptable version range using Maven/OSGi interval notation.
gherkinSteps: Given "[1.0.0,2.0.0)", When candidate 1.5.0 is checked, Then satisfies; 2.0.0 does not (exclusive upper).

requirements.feature: Module descriptor validation (request ≤ limit invariant)
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator, I want a module's resource request validated against its limit at construction time.
gherkinSteps: Given a ModuleDescriptor whose request exceeds limit, When constructed, Then IllegalArgumentException naming both values.

requirements.feature: Tiered isolation model (TIER_1/TIER_2/TIER_3)
requirements.userStory: As a module author, I want to declare an isolation tier per module.
requirements.statusDetail: Complete (enum); TIER_3 enforcement Partial — see gimle-os
requirements.testCoverageDetail: NONE directly (exercised indirectly via ModuleDescriptorParserTest, gimle-os's PortableJvmFlagsResourceLimiterTest)
gherkinSteps: Given isolation.tier: TIER_2, When parsed, Then the module requires a dedicated worker JVM.

requirements.feature: Kubernetes-shaped resource quantity parsing
requirements.userStory: As a module author, I want to write resource requests using Kubernetes-style quantity suffixes.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: Indirect via ModuleDescriptorTest, VesselSpecTest — NONE direct
gherkinSteps: Given ResourceSpec{memory:"128Mi", cpu:"250m"}, When memoryBytes()/cpuMillicores() called, Then 134217728 and 250 respectively.

requirements.feature: Tenant-scoped service export
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator, I want a module's exported service restricted to an explicit tenant allow-list.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: `ServiceExportTenantTest` (unrestricted permits any, restricted permits only listed, never permits untenanted caller, empty allow list permits no one)
gherkinSteps: Given ServiceExport{allowedTenantIds={"tenant-a"}}, When permitsTenant(Optional.of("tenant-b")), Then false.

requirements.feature: StatefulSet-shaped persistent volume declaration
requirements.userStory: As a module author building StatefulSet-kind workloads, I want to declare a persistent local-disk volume request in the module artifact.
requirements.statusDetail: Complete; volume declaration reshaped: the never-consumed mountPath field was dropped and an optional reclaimPolicy (Retain default) added
gherkinSteps: Given gimle-module.yaml declaring volume:{sizeBytes[,reclaimPolicy]}, When parsed, Then ModuleDescriptor.volume() is present with reclaimPolicy defaulting to RETAIN.

requirements.feature: Health probe configuration: probe classes, initial delay, and per-module interval/timeout/failure threshold
requirements.userStory: As a module author, I want liveness/readiness probe classes plus an initial delay before the first check, and my own probe interval, per-check timeout and consecutive-liveness-failure threshold, so that a module whose check legitimately runs longer than the worker default is not reported as broken on every tick.
requirements.statusDetail: Complete. Modified by GIMLE-725: the health: block originally carried only the probe classes and initialDelaySeconds, with interval, timeout and liveness failure threshold fixed worker-wide. It now also carries intervalSeconds, timeoutSeconds and failureThreshold; HealthProbes holds them as Optional<Duration>/OptionalInt with a compact constructor enforcing positive interval and timeout, non-negative initial delay and threshold >= 1, and the worker's own 1s/2s/3 remain the documented defaults when a manifest declares none.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: `ModuleDescriptorParserTest` (no_initial_delay leaves empty, parses seconds, negative/non-numeric throws) Extended by HealthProbesTest and ModuleDescriptorParserTest for the three added fields and every validation failure.
gherkinSteps: Given health:{liveness:..., initialDelaySeconds:30}, When parsed, Then HealthProbes.initialDelay() is 30s.
Given health: also declares intervalSeconds, timeoutSeconds and failureThreshold, When parsed, Then each is carried on HealthProbes.
Given health: declares none of the three, When parsed, Then each is empty and the worker's own defaults apply.
Given health: declares a zero or negative interval or timeout, or a failureThreshold below 1, When parsed, Then a GimleManifestException is thrown.

requirements.feature: Vessel hosting mode (plain-process workload)
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator, I want to run a plain runnable jar as its own OS process under the same scheduling/health/resource machinery as a module.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: `VesselSpecTest` (no probes/ports is valid, TCP readiness requires a declared port, fixed port allocation carries its number, negative fixed port rejected); VesselArtifacts NONE dedicated
gherkinSteps: Given a vessel: block declaring args/env/probe/resources, When validated, Then synthesized into a ModuleDescriptor always at TIER_2, no exports/hooks/volume; a TCP/HTTP probe with no declared port is rejected.

requirements.feature: Artifact-registry vs local-path reference resolution
requirements.userStory: As a platform developer, I want one convention (blank string = resolve from Andvari by coordinate) for artifact path travel.
gherkinSteps: Given artifactPath="", When ArtifactReference.isRegistryCoordinate is called, Then true, isLocalPath false.

requirements.feature: RBAC domain model (resources, verbs, permissions, roles, bindings)
requirements.userStory: As a cluster operator, I want a coarse but complete RBAC model, optionally tenant-scoped, granted via named roles.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: `PermissionTest` (unscoped covers any tenant, scoped only own tenant, mismatch never covers), `RoleBindingTest` (well-formed subject accepted, malformed rejected)
gherkinSteps: Given Permission scoped to (DEPLOYMENT,WRITE,tenant="acme"), When covers(DEPLOYMENT,WRITE,Optional.of("acme")), Then true; a different tenant, false.

requirements.feature: Built-in cluster-admin role and operator/node certificate groups
requirements.userStory: As a cluster operator upgrading to RBAC, I want every existing operator certificate to retain full access via an implicit cluster-admin binding.
gherkinSteps: Given BuiltinRoles.CLUSTER_ADMIN, When inspected, Then contains one unscoped Permission for every (ResourceKind,Verb) combination.

requirements.feature: Console password hashing (PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256)
requirements.userStory: As a cluster operator, I want console account passwords stored as salted PBKDF2 hashes, never plaintext.
gherkinSteps: Given a password hashed twice via PasswordHashes.hash, When compared, Then outputs differ but both verify against the original.

requirements.feature: Mutual-TLS SSLContext construction
requirements.userStory: As a platform component, I want to build an mTLS SSLContext from my own leaf cert/key plus the cluster CA in one call.
gherkinSteps: Given valid cert/key/CA PEM files, When SslContexts.forMutualTls(settings) is called, Then a TLS 1.3 handshake against a same-CA-trusting peer succeeds.

requirements.feature: Cluster-wide transport protocol switch (plaintext/TLS)
requirements.userStory: As a cluster operator, I want one system property/env var to switch every network-exposed transport between plaintext and TLS.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: `TransportProtocolTest`, `TlsSettingsTest` (defaults to plaintext, case-insensitive, rejects unrecognized value, fails fast on unset property)
gherkinSteps: Given -Dgimle.transport.protocol=tls, When TransportProtocol.fromConfig() is called, Then TLS; an unrecognized value throws.

requirements.feature: Stateless HMAC-signed console session tokens
requirements.userStory: As a console user, I want my login session represented as a self-verifying, stateless signed token.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: `SessionTokensTest` (issue_then_verify round trips, expired rejected, wrong-key rejected, tampered rejected, garbage input rejected not thrown)
gherkinSteps: Given a token issued with 5-minute TTL, When verified 1ms before expiry, Then succeeds; after expiry, tampered, or wrong-key-signed, returns empty.

requirements.feature: Session-signing key file load-or-create with owner-only permissions
requirements.userStory: As an operator standing up a console-serving process, I want its session-signing key auto-generated and persisted with owner-only permissions.
gherkinSteps: Given no key file exists, When loadOrCreate called twice, Then first generates rw------- key, second reuses it.

requirements.feature: Per-key exponential-backoff login throttle
requirements.userStory: As a cluster operator, I want repeated failed login attempts against one username or address throttled with exponential backoff.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: `LoginThrottleTest` (delay doubles up to cap, success clears history, keys tracked independently)
gherkinSteps: Given 3 failed attempts (threshold 3), When a 4th failure is recorded, Then throttledUntil(key) returns a future instant, doubling per failure up to a cap.

requirements.feature: Structured JSON log encoding with APPLICATION/PLATFORM categorization
requirements.userStory: As an operator querying logs programmatically, I want every log line self-describing JSON tagged with process role, node id, and (for hosted modules) deployment/instance identity.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: `JsonLogEncoderTest` (categorizes platform/application, tenant id included only when present, process role/node id read fresh)
gherkinSteps: Given a log event with deploymentName/instanceIndex MDC keys set, When encoded by JsonLogEncoder, Then category="APPLICATION" carrying moduleId/deploymentName/instanceIndex; without those, category="PLATFORM".

requirements.feature: Human-readable colored console log encoding
requirements.userStory: As a developer watching a process's terminal, I want log lines colored by level and tagged with [deployment#index].
gherkinSteps: Given -Dgimle.color=always, When encoded by TextLogEncoder, Then output contains ANSI escapes; -Dgimle.color=never produces none.

requirements.feature: Runtime-switchable console log format (text default, JSON opt-in)
requirements.userStory: As a platform developer, I want the console appender to default to colored text but be forceable to JSON.
requirements.statusDetail: Complete. The four properties `gimle-core` reads at startup -- `gimle.log.console`, `gimle.log.root`, `gimle.log.maxFileSizeBytes` and `gimle.log.maxFiles` -- are now documented with their defaults, the fact that an unrecognized console value silently falls back to text, and why console format is a presentation choice only: every process writes an unconditional JSON trail to its own platform log file through a separate appender this property never touches, and that file, not stdout, is what the Logs screen, `gimle logs` and Muninn all read. The one exception, a worker JVM its agent always spawns with `-Dgimle.log.console=json`, is documented with the reason (the agent tells structured lines from unstructured ones on the raw pipe). The two rotation properties are documented as applying to every rotated surface alike and as needing to be set consistently, since the readers behind `gimle logs` honour `gimle.log.maxFiles` too.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: `ConsoleLogEncoderTest` (explicit json/text override, no override defaults to text)
gherkinSteps: Given -Dgimle.log.console=json, When CONSOLE appender starts, Then delegates to JsonLogEncoder; no override defaults to text.

requirements.feature: MDC-tagged proxying for same-worker and probe-loop invocations
requirements.userStory: As a platform developer, I want a hosted module's service reference/probe callback automatically tagged with that instance's identity in the logging MDC.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: `InstanceMdcContextTest` (tag_proxy sets/restores MDC, restores on throw, run_tagged restores previous value)
gherkinSteps: Given a service reference wrapped via InstanceMdcContext.tagProxy, When a method throws, Then caller's MDC is restored to prior state, original exception propagates.

requirements.feature: Per-instance sifted log files
requirements.userStory: As an operator debugging one instance among many hosted in the same worker, I want that instance's own log lines routed to their own rotated file.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: `InstanceSiftingFileAppenderTest` (routes application lines by deployment/instance, skips platform lines, never leaks across instances, reopens after close)
gherkinSteps: Given two instances of different deployments logging concurrently, When both emit APPLICATION lines, Then each lands only in its own deployment-index.log file.

requirements.feature: Platform (non-instance) log file appender
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want a process's own component logs written to a dedicated rotated file separate from any hosted-instance output.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: Exercised via `LogRotationTest`; no dedicated unit test class
gherkinSteps: Given an APPLICATION event and a PLATFORM event, When both reach PlatformFileAppender, Then only the PLATFORM event is written.

requirements.feature: Kubelet-style size/count log rotation
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want log files rotated by size with a fixed number of retained copies, matching kubelet's semantics.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: `LogRotationTest` (rolls over by size and evicts oldest, cursor paging/follow resolve correctly across rotation)
gherkinSteps: Given small maxFileSizeBytes/maxFiles, When enough lines exceed the cap repeatedly, Then the oldest rotated copy is evicted past maxFiles.

requirements.feature: Cursor-based log paging and live-follow streaming
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want to page backward through historical log lines and live-tail via a stable timestamp cursor.
gherkinSteps: Given a log stream spanning a rotation, When streamFollow is called from a cursor before the rotation, Then every line after that cursor is streamed as NDJSON, including lines now in the rotated file.

requirements.feature: Startup banner rendering with terminal color/Unicode auto-detection
requirements.userStory: As an operator starting any Gimlé process, I want a branded startup banner falling back to ASCII on non-UTF-8 terminals.
gherkinSteps: Given -Dgimle.banner.enabled=false, When GimleBanner.print is called, Then nothing is written.

requirements.feature: Single-write length-prefixed wire framing
requirements.userStory: As a platform developer implementing a binary transport, I want a shared length-prefix framing helper that writes the length and body as one syscall to avoid Nagle-related latency.
gherkinSteps: Given a body byte array, When Frames.writeFrame(out, body) is called, Then exactly one write call places a 4-byte length prefix followed by the body, then flushes.

requirements.feature: Hand-rolled JSON parser/writer
requirements.userStory: As a platform developer, I want a minimal, dependency-free JSON reader/writer for the control plane's fixed, fully-known HTTP shapes.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: `JsonTest` (nested objects/arrays, negative/exponent numbers, escaped strings, round trip, escapes special chars, malformed throws)
gherkinSteps: Given a nested JSON document, When parsed then re-written via Json.write(Json.parse(text)), Then every value round-trips; malformed input throws IllegalArgumentException.

requirements.feature: Agent↔worker control-channel protocol and codec
requirements.userStory: As a platform developer, I want a simple, human-debuggable line-oriented protocol for the agent-worker control channel.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: `ControlMessageCodecTest` (module id with qualifier round trips, rejects empty line/unknown type/missing fields/malformed module id)
gherkinSteps: Given a ControlMessage.InstallModule with a free-text artifactPath containing a space, When encoded/decoded via ControlMessageCodec, Then field-for-field identical.

requirements.feature: Node registration/heartbeat/capacity-reporting protocol
requirements.userStory: As the control plane, I want each node agent to register supported isolation tiers/labels once and periodically report capacity/instance state.
gherkinSteps: Given a node registering with NodeCapabilities(supportedTiers={TIER_1,TIER_2}), When the scheduler considers a TIER_3 replica, Then rejected as a placement candidate.

requirements.feature: Instance lifecycle event log model
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want every instance's lifecycle transition recorded as a durable, stably-identified event with a compact cause summary on failure.
gherkinSteps: Given a TRANSITION_FAILED event, When constructed, Then it carries a non-empty causeSummary alongside a stable id.

requirements.feature: Cross-resource audit trail model
requirements.userStory: As a cluster operator, I want every authorization decision recorded as a durable, queryable audit entry.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: `AuditEventTest` (denied represented same as allowed, null groups/tenant/target coalesce to empty, blank id rejected)
gherkinSteps: Given a denied authorization decision, When recorded as an AuditEvent, Then allowed=false and otherwise structurally identical to an allowed one.

requirements.feature: Certificate bootstrap (CSR) request/response protocol
requirements.userStory: As a node agent or new human operator, I want a standard request/response shape for submitting a CSR.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: NONE direct (approval-policy logic in gimle-controlplane's ApiServer)
gherkinSteps: Given CsrSubmission with purpose=OPERATOR_CLIENT, When submitted, Then CsrResult status=PENDING with a requestId, never auto-approved.

requirements.feature: Assigned-instance work-order model (incl. in-place rename and vessel dispatch)
requirements.userStory: As a node agent, I want one work-order record per placement decision that also tells me whether it's a retarget or a vessel dispatch.
gherkinSteps: Given an AssignedInstance with renamedFromInstanceIndex present, When the agent processes it, Then it retargets the already-running instance under that prior index in place.

requirements.feature: Bounded-retry-with-backoff restart policy (CrashLoopBackOff-equivalent)
requirements.userStory: As the platform, I want one shared exponential-backoff-with-rolling-window retry policy for both module-level and worker-level restart decisions.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: `RestartTrackerTest` (allows retry within budget, exhausts after max attempts, delay grows exponentially/capped, window resets budget, success resets tracker)
gherkinSteps: Given a tracker with maxAttemptsPerWindow=3, When a 4th failure is recorded within the window, Then recordFailureAndCheckShouldRetry returns false.

requirements.feature: Tenant identity and resource quota model
requirements.userStory: As a cluster operator, I want each tenant to carry an explicit resource ceiling.
gherkinSteps: Given a Tenant with negative quota field, When constructed, Then rejected with IllegalArgumentException.

requirements.feature: Tenant-scoped config/secret entry model
requirements.userStory: As a module author, I want to read tenant-scoped config or secret values through one uniform record shape.
gherkinSteps: Given ConfigEntry{encrypted:true}, When constructed and value() accessed, Then a defensive clone is returned each time.

requirements.feature: Bundled SPA static-asset resolution from classpath
requirements.userStory: As a platform developer packaging a console frontend into a backend process's own jar, I want a shared mechanism to resolve the bundled SPA's static root whether running from a real jar or exploded classes.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: `BundledSpaTest` (file-scheme, jar-scheme, empty when absent, resolves different markers for different consoles)
gherkinSteps: Given a marker resource existing only inside a jar's entry, When BundledSpa.resolve(classLoader, markerResource) is called against a real built jar, Then it opens a jar filesystem and returns the marker's parent directory.

requirements.feature: SPA static file serving with client-side-route fallback
requirements.userStory: As a platform developer serving a built React SPA, I want unknown paths to fall back to the SPA shell (200), while a genuinely missing asset still 404s, with path-traversal/symlink-escape rejected.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: `SpaStaticHandlerTest` (serves real static file, falls back to shell, missing asset 404s, rejects traversal, rejects symlink escape)
gherkinSteps: Given a request for /some/client/route with no matching file, When handled by SpaStaticHandler, Then the SPA shell is returned with 200; /../etc/passwd is rejected with 400.

requirements.feature: Saga test-run event model and NDJSON codec
requirements.userStory: As a test-infrastructure maintainer, I want every test run's events shipped as an append-only, replayable NDJSON stream.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: `SagaEventCodecTest` (single line naming type first, absent fields omitted)
gherkinSteps: Given a TestFinished event with no failure fields, When encoded via SagaEventCodec, Then absent Optional failure fields are omitted, never written as null.

requirements.feature: Stable failure-signature hashing for flaky-test clustering
requirements.userStory: As a test-infrastructure maintainer, I want a stable, normalized hash of a failure's "shape" so the same underlying defect clusters under one signature across runs.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: `FailureSignatureTest` (run-specific numbers don't change signature, hex ids don't change it, different exception types differ, different messages differ, oversized messages truncated)
gherkinSteps: Given two failure messages differing only in an embedded port number, When both hashed via FailureSignature.of, Then identical signature; a genuinely different message produces a different one.

requirements.feature: Module dependency resolution with cycle detection
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator, I want a module's requires: declarations resolved to the highest satisfying installed version, with cycles rejected up front.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: `ModuleResolverTest` (wires to highest satisfying version, candidate must be resolved/active, unsatisfied requirement reported, 2/3-length cycle detected, diamond dependency not a cycle, independent dependents wire independently)
gherkinSteps: Given module A requires B and B requires A, When ModuleResolver.resolve(A) is called, Then GimleResolutionException naming the cycle.

requirements.feature: Module registry (install bookkeeping, idempotent re-install, content-mismatch rejection)
requirements.userStory: As the platform, I want one authoritative source of truth for installed modules, with identical re-install a no-op but content-mismatch rejected.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: `ModuleRegistryTest` (register stores as installed, idempotent identical re-register, rejects differing re-register, unknown module id throws, named transitions update state, mark_failed reachable)
gherkinSteps: Given module foo@1.0.0 already registered, When register is called again with identical sha256, Then no-op returning the same id; differing sha256 throws.

requirements.feature: Module lifecycle state machine (INSTALLED→RESOLVED→STARTING→ACTIVE→STOPPING→UNINSTALLED, plus FAILED/COMPLETED)
requirements.userStory: As the platform, I want a module driven through a strict lifecycle state machine — gating hooks abort/propagate synchronously, teardown hooks best-effort never blocking.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: `ModuleControllerTest` (full happy path, start before resolve illegal, stop before active illegal, resolve failure marks failed, uninstall rejects active module, force_failed transitions to failed, complete_succeeded/failed paths)
gherkinSteps: Given a module whose onStart hook throws, When ModuleController.start(id) is called, Then transitions to FAILED, emits TransitionFailed, and rethrows wrapped as GimleLifecycleException.

requirements.feature: Dynamic per-module-version JPMS ModuleLayer construction
requirements.userStory: As the platform, I want each resolved module version to get its own dedicated ModuleLayer/classloader, parented on the shared platform layer plus wired dependencies' layers.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: `ModuleLayerFactoryTest` (builds dependency-free layer, dependent layer calls into exported API, two versions get distinct layers, missing parent layer fails with GimleResolutionException)
gherkinSteps: Given two installed versions of the same module both resolved, When each built via ModuleLayerFactory.create, Then distinct ModuleLayer/ClassLoader instances.

requirements.feature: Unnamed-module readability grant for bundled hooks/probes
requirements.userStory: As a hosted-module author bundling my own ModuleLifecycleHooks/LivenessProbe/ReadinessProbe implementations, I want my module's layer granted readability to the platform's own unnamed module.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: gimle-worker's `RealBundledHookAndProbeInvocationTest`; this module's own `ModuleLayerFactoryTest` exercises the general mechanism
gherkinSteps: Given a real module jar bundling its own ModuleLifecycleHooks implementation declared "requires static com.gimle.module", When the module's layer is created, Then the hook class resolves and correctly implements the platform's interface at runtime.

requirements.feature: Classloader leak detection via PhantomReference
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator, I want the platform to detect when a disposed module's classloader was not actually garbage-collected within a configurable window.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: `LeakTrackerTest` (no leak when collected, leak reported when retained, wired through ModuleController reports no leak on clean stop)
gherkinSteps: Given a module's layer/loader is tracked after disposal and never released, When the tracking window elapses, Then a ModuleLeakDetected event fires naming the module id, survival duration, and (best-effort) retaining path.

requirements.feature: Repeated-redeploy flat-metaspace acceptance test
requirements.userStory: As the platform, I want a mandatory acceptance test that redeploys a module in a loop and asserts metaspace usage plateaus.
gherkinSteps: Given a module redeployed N times in a loop, When metaspace usage is sampled, Then samples plateau after warm-up.

requirements.feature: Best-effort leak retaining-path attribution via JFR OldObjectSample
requirements.userStory: As an operator diagnosing a detected leak, I want the platform to attempt identifying what's still holding a reference into the leaked module's packages.
gherkinSteps: Given a worker JVM launched with the gimle-leak-detection JFR recording enabled with path-to-gc-roots=true, When a real leak is detected, Then OldObjectSampleCorrelator reports a human-readable retaining chain; without that flag, it degrades to no path.

requirements.feature: Module lifecycle hooks (reflectively instantiated, JPMS-exported)
requirements.userStory: As a module author, I want to implement onInstall/onStart/onStop/onUninstall hooks instantiated reflectively by the platform.
gherkinSteps: Given a descriptor naming a real ModuleLifecycleHooks implementation in an exported package, When the module resolves, Then the hooks class is instantiated via its no-arg constructor and onInstall invoked.

requirements.feature: Job-kind run-to-completion hooks
requirements.userStory: As a module author building a batch workload, I want a single run(ctx) executed once to completion, reporting SUCCEEDED/FAILED.
gherkinSteps: Given an ACTIVE Job-kind module whose JobHooks.run returns SUCCEEDED, When ModuleController.complete(id, SUCCEEDED) is called, Then transitions straight to COMPLETED, emitting a Completed lifecycle event.

requirements.feature: Module context API (in-flight tracking, service lookup, config, data dir, control-plane relay)
requirements.userStory: As a hosted module's hook/probe code, I want one context object exposing request in-flight counting, service lookup/invoke, config, volume path, and a whitelisted control-plane relay.
gherkinSteps: Given a hook calls ctx.beginRequest() and never calls endRequest(), When ModuleController.stop is called, Then the drain wait blocks up to its deadline because inFlightCount() > 0.

requirements.feature: In-worker round-robin service registry with version-aware cutover
requirements.userStory: As a hosted module, I want the same-worker service registry to select among ready providers round-robin, atomically cutting over to a newer version once ready.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: `SimpleServiceRegistryTest` (round robins, prefers highest ready version, falls back while highest has none ready, round robins within preferred version, mark_unready excludes without removing); `HotRedeployTest#old_and_new_versions_coexist_with_dependents_pinned_to_their_own_wiring`
gherkinSteps: Given both v1 (draining, still ready) and v2 (freshly started, one ready) registered, When lookup is called repeatedly, Then every call routes to v2 exclusively once v2 has any ready entry.

requirements.feature: Cross-tier name-driven service invocation
requirements.userStory: As a module whose routing config names a target only as runtime strings, I want to invoke it by name through the service registry.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: `SimpleServiceRegistryTest` (invokes directly by name, unknown interface returns empty, wrong method name throws, rethrows application exception with real type, void method returns empty Optional)
gherkinSteps: Given a registered Greeter provider with method greet(String), When invokeByName("...Greeter",1,"greet",["java.lang.String"],["world"]) is called, Then invoked reflectively; a wrong method name throws rather than matching a different overload.

requirements.feature: Same-worker cross-module service publish/discover
requirements.userStory: As two hosted modules in the same worker JVM, I want the provider to publish a service and the consumer to look it up by interface type.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: `ServiceRegistryIntegrationTest` (consumer finds service, consumer finds nothing without a provider)
gherkinSteps: Given a provider registers a Greeter instance and a consumer resolves afterward, When the consumer calls ctx.lookupService(Greeter.class), Then finds the provider's instance directly.

requirements.feature: Graceful drain-then-dispose stop with deadline
requirements.userStory: As the platform, I want stop to wait for in-flight requests to drain up to a fixed deadline, never indefinitely.
gherkinSteps: Given a module whose in-flight counter never reaches zero, When stop is called with a drain timeout, Then stop still completes once the deadline passes.

requirements.feature: Hot redeploy (old/new version coexistence with pinned dependent wiring)
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator, I want to install a new version alongside the still-active old one, with existing dependents staying pinned to whichever version they originally wired to.
gherkinSteps: Given dependent D wired to dependency v1, and v2 is then installed/resolved, When D's wiring is inspected afterward, Then still wired to v1 unless explicitly re-resolved.

requirements.feature: gimle-module.yaml descriptor parsing and validation

requirements.statusDetail: Complete. Modified: a restart attempt that failed after `controller.stop(id)` had already driven the module through UNINSTALLED dead-ended -- the module was gone from the registry with nothing retrying it and no terminal state recorded anywhere, so the instance was simply stranded. A failed attempt now re-enters the same backoff loop (`restartModule` is called again from the attempt's own tail), bounded exactly as before by the tracker's budget. Budget exhaustion now escalates through `ModuleController#abandonFailed` rather than `forceFailed`: `forceFailed` requires the module to still be ACTIVE, which is precisely the case that no longer holds after an uninstall, so exhaustion could previously fail to record anything at all. `abandonFailed` marks the registry when the module is still known and always emits the `TransitionFailed` event -- the event, not the registry write, is what reaches the agent as `ModuleStateChanged("FAILED")` and lets the machine tier take over.

Then RestartTracker.recordSuccess() resets the backoff budget for the next failure cycle
Given the module never recovers and the restart budget (5 attempts / 60s window) is exhausted

And onModuleRestartBudgetExhausted is invoked, logging that the worker itself needs restarting

requirements.userStory: As the platform, I want the agent to build a fully-formed worker JVM command line (leak-detection JFR flag, `-XX:+ExitOnOutOfMemoryError`, scoped log root, `-XX:ErrorFile`, ResourceLimiter flags, banner suppression, forced JSON console logging, and -- when this node runs under `gimle.transport.protocol=tls` -- its own already-resolved `gimle.transport.protocol`/`gimle.tls.certFile`/`keyFile`/`caFile`) and spawn it via ProcessBuilder, so that every worker this agent supervises is consistently instrumented, crash-classifiable, and carries the same node identity for anything it terminates or dials on the wire.
requirements.statusDetail: Fixed (NET-5): a live-cluster QA pass against a real transport: mtls cluster found that `stableWorkerFlags()` forwarded only `gimle.fabric.defaultDenyCrossTenant`/`gimle.banner.enabled`/`gimle.log.console` to a spawned worker -- never `gimle.transport.protocol` or `gimle.tls.certFile`/`keyFile`/`caFile`. Since `TransportProtocol.fromConfig()`/`TlsSettings.fromConfig()` only ever read JVM system properties, which don't cross a `ProcessBuilder` spawn boundary, every worker JVM always resolved PLAINTEXT regardless of the cluster's real posture -- confirmed via `ps aux` showing zero TLS flags on live worker command lines, `gimle-gateway`'s own HttpsServer termination silently serving plaintext, and a live cross-worker `gimle-fabric` call succeeding over an unencrypted channel on the same nominally-mTLS cluster. `stableWorkerFlags()` now also forwards this agent's own already-resolved transport posture via a new `workerTlsFlags()` helper -- empty in plaintext mode, a zero-behavior-change no-op there -- mirroring the existing `gimle.fabric.defaultDenyCrossTenant` forwarding pattern. Safe unconditionally when TLS is on: `bootstrapCertificateIfNeeded` already runs to completion earlier in `main()`, before any worker is ever spawned, so the cert/key files `TlsSettings.fromConfig()` validates are guaranteed to exist.

requirements.feature: Tier 1 density — shared-worker reuse for multiple module instances
requirements.userStory: As the platform, I want up to MAX_TIER1_DENSITY (4) Tier 1 instances of the same tenant -- including several replicas of one deployment -- packed into one already-running worker JVM instead of always spawning a fresh one, so that classloader-level density is realized without a per-instance JVM cost.
requirements.statusDetail: Fixed: the previous connection-identity grouping meant packing never actually occurred for the ordinary case of several new Tier-1 instances arriving in the same reconcile tick (a scale-up, or a first reconcile after this agent restarts and finds a pile of pre-existing assignments) -- every instance in such a batch saw every sibling's WorkerConnection as still null (filled in asynchronously once each spawned worker's JVM actually connects) and so always spawned its own worker, regardless of the configured density cap or available shared-worker budget. findReusableTier1Worker now groups supervised by workerKey (set synchronously at construction time, either an instance's own key for a freshly spawned worker or its owning instance's key for one already packed) instead of by WorkerConnection identity, so a same-tick sibling is visible immediately. installIntoExistingWorker now handles packing onto a worker whose connection isn't open yet: it proceeds synchronously when already connected, and otherwise waits (bounded, 30s) on a dedicated thread for the owner's connection before sending the install sequence, the same never-block-the-poll-loop posture driveInstanceUp already takes for a freshly spawned worker's own owning instance. Modified. Density excluded two replicas of one deployment from ever sharing a worker, which defeats what TIER_1 is: classloader isolation with a shared crash domain, chosen deliberately over TIER_2. The exclusion was not a decision but a consequence -- the worker keyed its registry, layers, lifecycle state, schedulers, identities and exported services by module coordinate, and two replicas are the same coordinate by construction, so the second install read as an idempotent re-install of the first and the two would have shared one layer and one lifecycle state. A new `ModuleInstanceId` (gimle-core: the coordinate plus what distinguishes one replica from another) is now the runtime handle throughout `ModuleRegistry`, `ModuleController`, `ModuleWiring`, `ModuleLayerFactory`, `LifecycleEvent`, `LeakTracker`, `ServiceRegistry`/`SimpleServiceRegistry`, `WorkerRuntime`, `InstanceIdentityRegistry`, `FabricServer`/`FabricServiceRegistry`/`ServiceCatalog` and `WorkerMetrics`, and on the agent-worker control channel (`ControlMessage` install/resolve/start/stop/uninstall/rename and every report, encoded as `name@version|tenant/deployment#index`). The agent derives the same identity from the assignment it already holds and captures it at construction, so a rename -- which replaces the assignment in place -- keeps addressing the instance the worker actually installed. `findByModuleId` matches on it too, where a coordinate-only match would have handed one sibling's reports to the other. The density guard now refuses only the same placement arriving twice.

requirements.statusDetail: Complete. Fixed (M64): once `VesselProcessSupervisor` reported its restart budget exhausted, `AgentMain` removed the `SupervisedVessel` entry outright, so `reconcileVesselAssignment`'s own `!supervisedVessels.containsKey(key)` check read "never started" on the very next poll tick and handed the same still-assigned instance a brand-new supervisor with a brand-new `RestartTracker` -- contradicting the ERROR log ('exhausted its restart budget; giving up') within roughly one poll interval, repeated indefinitely for as long as the underlying failure (e.g. M64's own port- starvation race) kept recurring. Fixed by leaving the exhausted `SupervisedVessel` in place (marked via a new `restartBudgetExhausted` field) rather than removing it: `reconcileVesselAssignment` now declines to start a fresh supervisor for an unchanged assignment while that flag is set, giving up for real, and clears it only when `requiresVesselReplacement` finds the assignment has genuinely changed (a real rollout, the one thing that should get a clean budget again). `updateVesselHealth` keeps reporting the dead process as `FAILED` every tick since the entry is never removed, rather than silently vanishing from the heartbeat once given up.

requirements.feature: Etcd-Style Live Membership Change (AddServer/RemoveServer)
requirements.userStory: As a cluster operator, I want to grow or shrink the Raft cluster one server at a time while live.
requirements.statusDetail: Complete. Fixed alongside (M45): `RemoveServer`/`AddServer` never once succeeded against an original member, only against a peer that had itself just been added -- leaving a grown cluster with no way back down by removing an original. Root cause was in the RPC layer, not Raft consensus itself: `StoreNode#handleAddServer`/`handleRemoveServer` mapped *every* `GimleRaftException` (already-a-member, not-a-member, a membership change still in flight -- all real, deterministic answers a leader that genuinely evaluated the request already knows) onto the same `NotLeader` response `notLeaderResponse` builds from this node's own `leaderHint()`. A leader answering this way about its own request reports itself as the hint, so `StoreClient`'s leader-follow retry lands right back on the same node, hits the identical deterministic rejection again, and -- because every other configured endpoint just redirects back to that same leader too -- eventually exhausts the whole endpoint list and reports the generic `storeUnreachable` ("no reachable store leader could serve removeServer after retrying every endpoint"), hiding the real, actionable reason behind a message that reads as a routing failure. `handlePropose` right above it in the same file already drew exactly this distinction for a mutation's own precondition rejection (`MutationRejected`, not `NotLeader`) -- `addServer`/`removeServer` simply hadn't been brought in line with that precedent. Fixed by reusing `MutationRejected` for this case too (checked via `RaftNode#isLeader` at the moment of the catch) and having `StoreClient` throw the leader's own reason verbatim as `GimleRaftException#membershipChangeRejected`, rather than only detecting failure by exhausting every endpoint. Confirmed at the `RaftNode` level in isolation that a grow-then-remove-an-original sequence already converged correctly once done right (a real store process's own joiner *does* call `start()`, unlike the test-only shortcut that skips it) -- the bug was reproducible only once the real `StoreNode`/`StoreClient` RPC layer, not just `RaftNode`'s own API, was exercised.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: `RaftMembershipChangeTest#adding_a_server_joins_it_and_a_subsequent_mutation_still_commits`, `#a_second_membership_change_is_rejected_while_an_earlier_one_is_still_uncommitted`, `#removing_a_server_drops_it_from_the_peer_set_and_the_lone_remaining_node_still_commits`, `RaftClusterTest#a_three_node_cluster_grows_to_five_live_and_writes_continue_succeeding`, `#growing_to_four_then_removing_an_original_voter_converges_back_to_three_and_stays_healthy`, `#adding_a_voter_doing_real_work_removing_an_original_then_killing_the_leader_stays_healthy`; `StoreClientMembershipChangeTest#a_deterministic_rejection_from_the_real_leader_reports_its_real_reason_not_unreachable`, `#grows_to_four_then_removes_an_original_peer_through_the_real_client_and_protocol` (the real `StoreClient`/`StoreNode`/`RaftNode` wire path, over real sockets, the layer M45's own bug actually lived in)
gherkinSteps: Given a running 3-node cluster with a leader; When addServer is called for a new peer; Then a self-inclusive MembershipChange entry is replicated, and a subsequent mutation still commits once the new node acknowledges; a second membership change is rejected while the first is uncommitted.

Reworked from the original YAML-file-per-resource write-through engine to etcd's persistence shape: StateStore is purely in-memory; RaftLog rides a segment-based WriteAheadLog (one fsync per appended record, explicit truncation records so a discarded suffix stays discarded across a crash, crash-torn tail discarded on open, any other damage refuses to load, whole-segment compaction under the snapshot floor); a freshly elected leader appends a no-op entry at its own term so committed entries re-apply immediately on a quiet cluster.

requirements.feature: Same-Worker Direct Invocation Tier
requirements.userStory: As a hosted module, I want a service call to a provider in my own worker JVM served as a direct in-JVM method call.

gherkinSteps: Given a provider in a different worker on the same node; When lookup resolves to that endpoint; Then the call is dispatched over a UDS (always plaintext).

requirements.feature: Cross-Machine TCP Invocation Tier
requirements.userStory: As a hosted module, I want a call to a provider on a different machine dispatched over TCP (optionally TLS).
gherkinSteps: Given a provider on a different node's worker; When lookup resolves to that endpoint; Then the call is dispatched over TCP, TLS when configured.

requirements.userStory: As a platform operator, I want the fabric to prefer same-machine endpoints but spill into remote once every same-machine candidate is busier than the least-loaded remote one.
gherkinSteps: Given several same-machine endpoints saturated and a remote endpoint with spare capacity; When lookup selects a candidate; Then the remote tier is admitted; when a same-machine endpoint is idle, remote is never consulted.

requirements.feature: Least-Outstanding-Requests Selection
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator, I want traffic within a candidate tier routed to the endpoint with fewest outstanding requests, ties broken round-robin.
gherkinSteps: Given two candidates, one busier; When select is called; Then the less-loaded candidate is chosen; ties round-robin.

requirements.feature: Per-Endpoint Circuit Breaker
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator, I want each remote endpoint protected by its own sliding-window error-rate circuit breaker.
gherkinSteps: Given an endpoint's error rate crosses errorRateThreshold; When another call is attempted; Then the breaker opens and excludes it; after cooldown it half-opens for one trial call.

requirements.feature: Circuit Breaker Exponential Cooldown Backoff
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator, I want each consecutive re-open to double the effective cooldown (capped at 16x).
gherkinSteps: Given a breaker that re-opens repeatedly; When each re-open occurs; Then the cooldown doubles up to a ceiling; a successful half-open trial resets it.

requirements.feature: Panic-Mode Ejection Floor
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator, I want lookup to stop excluding open-breaker endpoints once more than a configured fraction are ejected.
gherkinSteps: Given a lookup whose candidates are more than maxEjectionPercent open-breaker; When selectAllowedCandidate runs; Then every candidate is admitted back in; no known exporter anywhere still throws GimleClusterException.

requirements.feature: Application-Exception vs Transport-Failure Breaker Scoring

gherkinSteps: Given a remote endpoint whose method throws an application exception; When the call completes with InvokeError; Then the breaker records a success; only genuine transport failures count against it.

requirements.feature: Gossip-Propagated Service Catalog

gherkinSteps: Given a local registration on one catalog; When its payload is applied to a second catalog's onReceived; Then the second reflects the registration; a stale delta at a lower version is ignored.

requirements.feature: Catalog Eviction on Gossip-Detected Node Death

gherkinSteps: Given a member gossip converges on as DEAD; When ServiceCatalog#onMembershipChange receives it; Then endpointsForInterface no longer returns any of its endpoints; once ALIVE again, endpoints reappear with no re-registration.

requirements.feature: Cross-Tenant Service Export Access Control

gherkinSteps: Given a node already running Tier 2 instances for tenant A; When a Tier 2 replica for tenant B is scheduled; Then that node is excluded; if every candidate hosts a different tenant, placement fails outright.

requirements.feature: DaemonSet eligible-node enumeration (`eligibleNodes`)

requirements.feature: Deployment replica reconciliation (level-triggered)

requirements.feature: Tenant quota drift detection (`QuotaReconciler`)
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator, I want a deployment marked quota-violating whenever its tenant's actual usage exceeds quota, without automatic eviction.
requirements.statusDetail: Complete. Modified: `QuotaReconciler` skipped any workload whose tenant was not `Tenant#isEnforceable`, which excludes the `default` tenant by name -- so a quota an operator explicitly set on `default` was stored and reported back but never accumulated and never found violating. Both the usage accumulation and the violation verdict now key on whether the workload names a tenant at all, so the constraint's own existence decides what is enforced rather than the tenant's name.
gherkinSteps: Given a tenant's quota is lowered below already-running usage; When QuotaReconciler ticks; Then affected deployments are marked quota-violating with no instances evicted.

requirements.feature: JobRun run-to-completion reconciliation

requirements.feature: Job active-deadline enforcement

requirements.feature: CronJob schedule-driven Job materialization
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want a CronJob's schedule to automatically materialize a real Job at each due time.
requirements.statusDetail: Complete. Modified: the stored last-schedule value this reconciler maintains is a cursor over the schedule, not a record of anything having run -- it is stamped with the current time the first time a CronJob is reconciled at all, and keeps advancing past every instant that comes due while the CronJob is suspended. It was reported to operators as `lastScheduleTime`, so a CronJob that had never generated a single Job claimed a firing. The cursor is now reported as `scheduleEvaluatedThrough`, and `lastScheduleTime` is derived from the generated Jobs themselves; the reconciler's own cursor semantics are unchanged.
gherkinSteps: Given a CronJobSpec with schedule "* * * * *" and no prior lastSchedule; When first ticked; Then baseline is recorded with no retroactive burst; on the next due tick a Job named "{name}-{epochSeconds}" is materialized.
And the cursor this reconciler maintains is reported as `scheduleEvaluatedThrough`, never as a claim that a Job was generated.

requirements.feature: CronJob concurrency policy (Allow/Forbid/Replace)
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want to control overlapping CronJob firings via concurrency semantics.
gherkinSteps: Given the previous firing is still non-terminal and concurrencyPolicy=FORBID; When a new firing is due; Then it is skipped and logged.

requirements.feature: CronJob manual trigger (`gimle cronjob trigger`)
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want to fire a CronJob on demand independent of its schedule.
requirements.statusDetail: Complete. Fixed: the trigger sub-route's own tenant resolution (resolveCronJobNameOrHandleSubRoute) used workloadTenantHint, which blindly defaults an omitted ?tenant= to the literal "default" tenant rather than searching -- inconsistent with the plain GET/DELETE branch for the identical CronJob name, which already resolves a bare name via a real cross-tenant search. An untenanted trigger call against two tenants' same-named CronJob could therefore fire a different tenant's job than a GET/DELETE of the same bare name would have resolved. Now shares the identical declaredOrExistingTenant + findTenantByName(listCronJobSpecs) resolution GET/DELETE already use (see GIMLE-657), including the same AmbiguousTenantException 400 on a genuine name collision.
gherkinSteps: Given a CronJob exists; When POST /cronjobs/{name}/trigger is called; Then a Job is materialized immediately, and cronJobLastSchedule is left untouched.

requirements.feature: CronJob missed-schedule starting-deadline handling

gherkinSteps: Given a firing's startingDeadline is exceeded by processing time; When CronJobReconciler ticks; Then the firing is logged as missed with no Job materialized.

gherkinSteps: Given a deployment is deleted but its assignments remain; When the reconciler ticks; Then every assignment is removed.

gherkinSteps: Given multiple ApiServer replicas share one store cluster; When each replica's leaseTick runs; Then only the lease-holder executes the reconcile tick.

gherkinSteps: Given module-info.java for com.gimle.controlplane; When compiled/linked with jlink; Then only schedule/reconcile/api/pki/top-level packages are exported.

requirements.feature: Admission chain extension point
requirements.userStory: As a platform maintainer, I want admission checks run as an ordered, pluggable chain rather than hardcoded inline.
gherkinSteps: Given a chain with a rejecting plugin followed by an allowing plugin; When admit() runs; Then processing short-circuits at the first rejection; a later plugin sees an earlier plugin's mutated spec.

requirements.feature: Tenant resource quota admission check
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator, I want a Deployment, Job, DaemonSet, or StatefulSet submission rejected outright if it would push its tenant past its quota (accounting for surge headroom on a Deployment, and each kind's own peak committed-instance count via WorkloadResourceProfile).
requirements.statusDetail: Complete -- generalized from Deployment-only to every placeable WorkloadSpec kind (Deployment/Job/DaemonSet/StatefulSet) so a tenant can no longer bypass its quota by submitting a Job/DaemonSet/StatefulSet instead of a Deployment. Modified: the check gated on `Tenant#isEnforceable`, which excludes the `default` tenant by name, so a quota an operator explicitly set on `default` was accepted, reported back, and never applied to a single submission. Every tenant that exists is now charged against the quota stored for it, `default` included. The two rejections that are not a measured overage -- an absent tenant row, an artifact the control plane cannot read -- stay narrowed to a deliberately-named tenant (`unverifiable`), since refusing an untenanted workload for a jar that only ever has to exist on the node running it would break the ordinary local `artifactPath` path; the instance-count dimension, which needs no descriptor, is still checked even then.
gherkinSteps: Given tenant T's quota is nearly exhausted; When a submission with maxCommittedInstances (replicas+maxSurge) would exceed it; Then admission rejects with 409.

requirements.feature: Organization-specific policy-as-data admission (`policy.maxReplicasPerDeployment`)
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator, I want a per-tenant ceiling on replicas-per-deployment via ordinary config.
requirements.statusDetail: Complete. Modified: the plugin gated on `Tenant#isEnforceable`, so a `policy.maxReplicasPerDeployment` written against the `default` tenant was stored and never checked. The presence of the config entry is now the only thing that decides -- writing the key against `default` is as deliberate an act as writing it against a named tenant.
gherkinSteps: Given tenant T has policy.maxReplicasPerDeployment=10; When a submission requests 15 replicas; Then admission rejects citing the ceiling.

requirements.feature: Registry-coordinate artifact admission (Andvari integration)
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want a coordinate-only deployment admitted only if Andvari confirms the artifact exists.
gherkinSteps: Given a manifest names moduleId:version with no artifactPath, and Andvari doesn't have it; When submitted; Then admission rejects with 400; if Andvari is merely unreachable, admission still accepts with no recorded digest (level-triggered tolerance).

requirements.feature: PUT-time re-tenanting double-authorization
requirements.userStory: As a platform security owner, I want moving a resource between tenants to require write access under both tenants.
requirements.statusDetail: Complete. Fixed a real regression from the tenant-scoped-keying refactor (FUNC-23), which removed this guard on the reasoning that a re-tenanting write could no longer *corrupt* a different tenant's own stored copy (each is keyed independently) -- true, but beside the point GIMLE-249 actually protects: a caller holding write access to exactly one tenant could still conjure a same-named resource under a tenant it has no access to at all, confusing anyone who reads/deletes that bare name later expecting the tenant they know about. dispatchResourceRequest's PUT branch now runs a new requireDoubleAuthorizedForRetenanting check, once ordinary write authorization against the submitted tenant already passed: if the name currently exists under one or more *different* tenants (via the same existingTenant lookup GET/DELETE already use, unwrapping AmbiguousTenantException into its own tenant list when more than one other tenant already collides), the caller must hold a real WRITE grant on every one of those too, or the write is refused with 403 naming which tenant is still needed. Applies uniformly across Deployment/Job/CronJob/DaemonSet/StatefulSet (dispatchResourceRequest is shared by all five). Plaintext mode is explicitly exempted, matching requireAuthorizedForWrite's own carve-out -- there is no identity to check in that mode, and calling Authorizer.authorize with the synthetic anonymous principal would otherwise turn every plaintext re-tenanting write into a spurious, unconditional 403.

gherkinSteps: Given deployment D belongs to tenant A; When a caller with write access only to tenant B PUTs D with tenantId=B; Then the request is rejected unless the caller also has write access to tenant A.

Given the same setup but the caller holds write access to both tenant A and tenant B; When the identical PUT is submitted; Then it succeeds, tenant A's own copy survives untouched, and tenant B gets its own new copy.

requirements.feature: `gimle-system` reserved-tenant operator-only guard
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator, I want the reserved `gimle-system` tenant accessible only by `gimle:operators`-group callers.
requirements.statusDetail: Complete. Modified twice in the same pass. A plaintext caller previously resolved to no principal at all on this path, so the operator-group membership check had no subject to answer for and the reserved-tenant veto simply did not engage -- anyone could write, deploy into, or dry-run against `gimle-system` over plaintext. A caller presenting no credential now resolves to an explicit `anonymous` principal belonging to no group, so the veto engages and refuses it, and every audit row written in that mode has a name to attribute the write to. The second half corrects the overreach that first fix would have carried: privilege follows the credential, not the transport. `callerIdentity` now resolves whatever credential the request actually presented -- a session cookie or bearer token is honoured on a plaintext connection exactly as `resolvePrincipal` already honours it on the same request -- and falls back to the anonymous principal only when nothing at all was presented. Presenting no credential is what must never confer privilege.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: Exercised within `ApiServerAuthzTest`'s broader RBAC test set `ApiServerTest#a_plaintext_caller_cannot_write_or_delete_the_reserved_system_tenant`, `#a_plaintext_caller_cannot_deploy_into_the_reserved_system_tenant`, `#a_plaintext_dry_run_into_the_reserved_system_tenant_reports_the_refusal`, `#a_plaintext_caller_holding_an_operator_session_may_write_the_reserved_system_tenant`, `#a_plaintext_session_without_the_operator_group_still_cannot_write_it`. `gimle-smoke-tests`' `GreeterSmokeClusterSupport` now logs in as the operator account it already creates before writing the reserved tenant, instead of relying on plaintext bypassing the veto.
gherkinSteps: Given a caller holds a broad but non-operator-group grant; When writing under tenantId=gimle-system; Then rejected 403 regardless of ordinary RBAC outcome.
Given a caller presenting no credential at all, over plaintext transport
When it writes, deletes or deploys under tenantId=gimle-system
Then it is refused, while a plaintext caller holding an operator session is admitted

requirements.feature: Dual audit logging for push/delete decisions
requirements.userStory: As a compliance auditor, I want every artifact push and delete decision durably recorded, both as a log line and a queryable AuditEvent.
requirements.statusDetail: Complete. Modified: plaintext mode returned from the authorization helper before either audit half ran, so a push or delete received that way left no trace in this process's own log at all -- and an unauthenticated push is precisely the case where the trail matters, since it places an executable jar where agents will run it. Both halves are now written in that mode too, attributed to the same synthetic `anonymous` principal this server's own session endpoint already reports there. Both also now name the affected `moduleId:version` coordinate and the artifact's tenant: without it the trail could prove that someone deleted something and when, but not which artifact, which under concurrent pushes leaves timestamp correlation as the only way to find out. The SLF4J line is written first, so the coordinate reaches an operator's log even when the durable append cannot reach the store. Reads (pulls) are still not durably audited.
sourceLocations: `gimle-andvari/src/main/java/com/gimle/andvari/AndvariServer.java` (`recordAudit` with target and tenant, plaintext-mode audit)
requirements.testCoverageDetail: Exercised via `AndvariServerTlsTest`'s auth test set `AndvariServerAuditTest#a_push_and_a_delete_are_both_logged_and_durably_recorded_against_their_coordinate` covers the plaintext path and the coordinate directly.
gherkinSteps: Given a push or delete is attempted; When authorizeArtifacts completes; Then a SLF4J line and a durable AuditEvent are both recorded — reads (pulls) are not durably audited.
Given the registry is running in plaintext mode; When a jar is pushed or a version deleted; Then both audit halves are still written, naming the coordinate and the artifact's tenant.

requirements.feature: Windows-safe on-disk path sanitization for colon-bearing processId

requirements.statusDetail: Complete. Modified: the `_`-for-`:` substitution was lossy, and a process id may itself contain `_`, so nothing could recover the original id from a directory name. That was fine while every read took its process id from the request URL, and became a real limit the moment a cross-process trace search had only a directory listing to read it from -- a lossy name would leave it unable to say which process a span it found actually ran on. The escape is now the percent-shaped, reversible `%3A` (a process id never contains `%`), with `decodeProcessId` its exact inverse.
gherkinSteps: Given a subtreePath containing a literal colon (e.g. "metrics/CONTROLPLANE/127.0.0.1:8080")
When lines are appended and then read back
Then the write succeeds by substituting "_" for ":" in the on-disk directory name only
And the returned data's processId (from the URL, never the directory name) is unchanged
And a process id containing both `_` and `:` is recovered exactly from its own directory name

requirements.feature: Gateway HTTP server bootstrap via module lifecycle hooks
requirements.userStory: As the gateway module, I want its listen port and route table read from `ModuleContext#config(...)` and a plain `HttpServer` bound on `onStart`, torn down on `onStop`, so it participates in the platform's own module lifecycle rather than needing external process management.
requirements.statusDetail: Modified. `onStart` now requires `gateway.port` and `gateway.controlPlaneEndpoint`, binds its listener with an empty route table, and lets the first reload tick fetch the declared Ingresses -- rather than parsing a `gateway.routes` config value. M43 fix: a re-run of `hilmir up --machine X` against a machine with some roles already alive used to respawn every role unconditionally -- including a second, fully live node-agent racing the original over worker ownership -- and overwrote its own run ledger with only the freshly-spawned pids, permanently losing all record of the still-alive originals. `up` now checks each role's own genuine liveness (process-table alive and, where the role carries a readiness address, still answering there) before respawning, skips any role already running, and its ledger write for the re-run keeps every skipped role's real, original pid alongside any freshly-spawned replacement rather than overwriting it.

requirements.statusDetail: Complete. M42 fix: `status` used to report `alive=true` for a pid the OS process table still lists even once it is a killed process's own zombie entry the OS hasn't reaped yet -- a naive `ProcessHandle#isAlive()` check alone cannot tell a zombie from a genuinely running process. `status` now also weighs the record's own readiness probe: a pid the process table still shows alive is reported dead once its own readiness address (already confirmed open at the moment `up` recorded it) is found closed, since a role's readiness can only regress from open to closed by actually dying, never by merely still starting.
gherkinSteps: Given a run ledger from a prior "hilmir up", When "hilmir down --machine m1", Then every process (and descendants) killed in reverse spawn order and the ledger deleted; status against a never-run machine reports a clean error.

requirements.feature: Secrets browsing/reveal/version/write/destroy (vault-native UI)
requirements.userStory: As a vault operator, I want to browse secrets, reveal values, view version history, write new versions, and soft-/hard-delete a key.
requirements.statusDetail: Fixed: two QA-found bugs, both confined to this screen. (1) "Reveal value" crashed the whole Secrets page: HttpSecretsRepository#versions declared its return type as number[], but GET .../versions actually returns an array of {version, author, writtenAtEpochMilli, type} objects -- the version-picker's own `<option key={version} value={version}>v{version}</option>` then tried to render one of those objects as a raw JSX child for every stored version, three uncaught React error #31s for a secret with three versions and a full-page error boundary. versions() (and the SecretsRepository contract) now returns the real per-version objects; every caller renders `.version` explicitly, and SecretValue/RevealedSecret carry the API's `type` field too rather than discarding it. (2) "Write new version" had no type field at all: every PUT always omitted `type`, which Fafnir's own SecretType#fromWire(null) treats as opaque, so writing a new version of an existing pem-certificate/pem-private-key secret silently downgraded its declared type with no shape validation ever run -- a value with no BEGIN CERTIFICATE marker corrupted a certificate secret undetected. SecretDialog now resolves and shows the secret's currently-declared type before opening (via versions(), without revealing its plaintext), defaults to it so a plain write preserves the type, lets an operator deliberately pick a different one, and runs the same structural PEM-marker check Fafnir's own SecretType#validate applies (src/lib/secretType.ts#pemProblem) client-side before submit -- on top of, not instead of, the server's own authoritative re-check once the correct type is actually sent.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: `src/repositories/secrets.test.ts` (MockSecretsRepository versions()/upsert() type handling and PEM rejection), `src/repositories/http/secrets.test.ts` (versions() returns the API's full per-version objects, read()/upsert() carry type), `src/stores/useSecretsStore.test.ts` (new: reveal() stores real per-version objects rather than bare numbers, currentType() resolves the latest version's declared type, save() sends the caller's declared type through to the write)
gherkinSteps: Given a secret has 3 versions, When I view its history, Then all versions are listed with the latest flagged; "destroy" permanently removes it.

Given a pem-certificate-typed secret, When "Write new version" is opened, Then its current type is shown and preselected, and a value with no BEGIN CERTIFICATE marker is refused client-side before it can reach the server.
