gherkinSteps: Given a healthy gimle-mimir replica reachable at its configured --health-port; When GET /health is called; Then it answers 200 with this replica's own isLeader/leaderHint/memberCount.
Given a control plane whose gimle-mimir cluster is unreachable; When GET /health is called; Then it answers 503 rather than 200, failing closed on the downstream outage.
Given a node agent's always-on log-serving HTTP surface; When GET /health is called; Then it answers 200 with no configuration needed, regardless of whether the opt-in admin fault API is enabled.

requirements.feature: Audit-trail ring-buffer eviction is observable: logged, counted, and surfaced in the GET /audit response
requirements.userStory: As a cluster operator relying on the audit trail during an incident, I want to know when the trail has silently degraded from a complete record to only its most recent 50,000 events, so I don't mistake a truncated trail for a complete one exactly when I most need to trust it.
requirements.statusDetail: Fixed: closes FUNC-46 -- StateStore.putAuditEvent's ring-buffer eviction (while (auditEvents.size() > MAX_AUDIT_EVENTS) auditEvents.remove(0)) discarded the oldest event with no log line, no counter, and no way for a caller to tell it had ever happened; GET /audit returned a bare array with no total count, oldest-retained timestamp, or truncation flag. StateStore now tracks a running auditEventsEvictedTotal (guarded by the same lock as the trail itself), logs a throttled warning (first eviction, then every 1000th) once the cap is first reached, and exposes both plus the current retained count and oldest-retained timestamp via a new AuditTrailStatus record and StoreReader#auditTrailStatus() -- wired through a new StoreRpc.GetAuditTrailStatus/AuditTrailStatusResult RPC pair to StoreClient#auditTrailStatus(). ApiServer's GET /audit response changed from a bare events array to an envelope ({events, retainedCount, evictedTotal, oldestRetainedAtEpochMilli?, truncated}) describing the whole trail's retention state independent of whatever filter/limit a given query applied -- gimle-cli's AuditCommand prints a note when truncated, and the console's Audit screen renders a banner.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: Full gimle-mimir (574 tests), gimle-controlplane (606 tests), and gimle-cli (120 tests) module suites re-verified against the new envelope shape and every call site that parses GET /audit's body (gimle-holmgang's ClusterApi, ApiServerCustomKindsTest) was updated to match. No dedicated new eviction-at-50000-events test in this pass (impractical to run at full scale in a unit test); the envelope shape itself is exercised end to end by the updated call sites.
gherkinSteps: Given the audit trail has exceeded MAX_AUDIT_EVENTS; When the next event is appended; Then the oldest event is evicted, a warning is logged (throttled after the first), and the trail's own evictedTotal counter increments.

Given a truncated audit trail; When an operator calls GET /audit (with any filter); Then the response envelope's truncated flag is true and evictedTotal/retainedCount describe the whole trail, independent of the filter applied.
Given gimle-cli's audit list command against a truncated trail; When the command completes; Then it prints a note naming how many events were discarded, alongside the filtered results.

requirements.feature: Password hashes carry their own iteration count, so raising PasswordHashes.ITERATIONS never breaks an existing hash
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator, I want raising the PBKDF2 iteration count later (to track a rising OWASP floor, as this exact value already once did) to never invalidate every previously-stored account password hash, so a floor increase can be absorbed incrementally instead of forcing a mass account reset.
requirements.statusDetail: Fixed: closes FUNC-76 -- PasswordHashes.ITERATIONS was a hardcoded constant and the stored format was salt || hash only, with no record of which iteration count actually produced a given hash; verify() always re-derived at today's constant. Raising ITERATIONS later would have made every previously-stored hash stop verifying immediately, with no migration path. The wire format is now iterations || salt || hash: hash() always stamps today's ITERATIONS, and verify() re-derives using the count embedded in the hash itself, never today's constant -- so a hash minted under a lower historical count keeps verifying correctly after the constant rises. Added needsRehash(byte[]), returning true when a hash's embedded count is below today's ITERATIONS, for a caller that just verified a password to optionally re-hash-and-store it at the current count and absorb the upgrade incrementally.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: PasswordHashesTest gained verify_still_succeeds_against_a_hash_produced_at_a_lower_iteration_count (hand-builds an old-count hash via the same PBKDF2WithHmacSHA256 primitive, independent of PasswordHashes' own hash()), plus needsRehash coverage for a today's-count hash, a lower-count hash, and a malformed blob. Full gimle-core (156 tests), gimle-pki (30 tests), gimle-controlplane (606 tests), gimle-fafnir (189 tests), and gimle-andvari module suites re-verified against the changed wire format -- every PasswordHashes.hash()/verify() call site in those modules round-trips through the new format transparently.
gherkinSteps: Given a password hash produced under an older, lower iteration count; When PasswordHashes.ITERATIONS is later raised; Then verify() against that old hash still succeeds, re-deriving at the count embedded in the hash rather than today's constant.
Given a password hash produced at today's iteration count; When needsRehash is called on it; Then it reports false.

Given a password hash produced at a lower iteration count; When needsRehash is called on it after a successful verify; Then it reports true, signaling the caller may re-hash-and-store at today's count.

requirements.feature: A group: RoleBinding subject now authorizes a session-cookie-authenticated (console/CLI-login) principal, not only a certificate-authenticated one
requirements.userStory: As a cluster operator, I want a `group:` RoleBinding to grant access to any console-login account currently carrying that group, so I can manage access by group membership for browser-based operators the same way I already can for mTLS-authenticated ones.
requirements.statusDetail: Fixed: closes FUNC-67 -- every session-cookie-authenticated Principal (ApiServer, FafnirServer, AndvariServer) was constructed with a hardcoded empty Set.of() for its groups, so a `group:` RoleBinding subject could never match a console-login (username/password) caller, only a certificate-authenticated one whose groups come from its client certificate's O= RDN. Account (gimle-core) gained a `groups` field, DomainCodec gained wire serialization for it, and each server's resolvePrincipal now reads the account's current groups live from the store per request (never baked into the session token, which carries only username -- so a group change takes effect on the caller's very next request, no re-login needed) rather than defaulting to Set.of(). ApiServer's PUT /accounts/{username} accepts an optional `groups` array; omitting it preserves the account's existing groups (a console password-only reset can no longer silently strip group membership), and accountToJson/principalToJson expose it. gimle-cli's `set account` gained --groups, and the console's Accounts screen gained a Groups column and editable comma-separated groups field.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: ApiServerAuthzTest gained group_role_binding_authorizes_a_session_authenticated_principal, proving end to end: a group-bound RoleBinding grants a session-authenticated account carrying that group, denies one without it, and both revokes and grants access live (no re-login) when the store-side account's groups change mid-session. ApiServerAccountManagementTest gained coverage for groups round-tripping through PUT/GET, the password-hash never leaking, groups preserved when omitted from a reset, replaced when given explicitly, and cleared with an empty array. gimle-console gained accounts.test.ts/http/accounts.test.ts coverage for the same preserve-vs-replace behavior and the groups wire payload.
gherkinSteps: Given a Role bound to `group:qa-team` granting DEPLOYMENT:READ, and an Account with groups=["qa-team"]; When that account logs in via the console and requests GET /deployments; Then the request is authorized.
Given the same setup but an Account with no groups; When it requests GET /deployments; Then the request is denied with 403.

Given an already-logged-in session for an account currently in `qa-team`; When an operator removes that account's groups via PUT /accounts/{username} with an explicit empty groups array; Then the very next request on that same session is denied, with no re-login required.
Given an account with groups=["qa-team"]; When its password is reset via PUT /accounts/{username} with only {password} (no groups field); Then its group membership is unchanged.

requirements.feature: The console's Metrics and Instances screens surface per-instance error rate, which the control plane already shipped on the wire but no console type or screen ever read
requirements.userStory: As a cluster operator, I want to see each instance's and each deployment's observed error rate on the Metrics and Instances screens, so I can spot an erroring workload without cross-referencing raw API responses by hand.
requirements.statusDetail: Fixed: closes FUNC-09 -- ApiServer#observationToJson has always included errorRatePerSecond in InstanceObservation's wire JSON, but the console's InstanceObservation/ModuleInstance TypeScript interfaces never declared the field, and every Http*Repository (deployments/daemonsets/statefulsets/instances) that maps that raw JSON into typed objects silently dropped it in the process -- so no screen could read it even though the data was present on every response. Added errorRatePerSecond to the shared InstanceObservation/ModuleInstance types, threaded it through every Raw*Instance mapping and UNOBSERVED default, and surfaced it: the Instances table gained an err/s column (highlighted when nonzero), the instance detail page gained an Error rate stat, and the Metrics screen gained a total-error-rate stat tile, an 'Instances with errors' ranked panel, and error-rate-aware coloring on the request-rate/queue-depth backpressure scatter.
sourceLocations: `gimle-console/src/routes/metrics.tsx` (error-rate stat tile, Instances with errors panel, scatter coloring)
requirements.testCoverageDetail: HttpDeploymentsRepositoryTest gained a dedicated errorRatePerSecond pass-through assertion; HttpInstancesRepositoryTest's flatten regression test now asserts errorRatePerSecond survives the flatten step that previously dropped it; MockAccountsRepository-style UNOBSERVED default assertions in deployments/statefulsets/daemonsets tests updated to include the zeroed field. Full gimle-console Vitest suite (294 tests) re-verified green.
gherkinSteps: Given a deployment instance whose control-plane observation reports errorRatePerSecond=3.5; When the console's Instances screen loads that deployment's rows; Then the err/s column for that instance shows 3.50 and is visually flagged.
Given the same instance; When the console's Metrics screen loads; Then the deployment appears in the 'Instances with errors' panel and contributes to the total error-rate stat tile.

requirements.feature: A declarative AlertRule primitive: a threshold on one deployment's observed signal that posts a webhook notification when crossed and again when resolved
requirements.userStory: As a cluster operator, I want to declare a threshold on a deployment's request rate, error rate, queue depth, CPU, or memory usage and be notified via webhook when it's crossed (and again when it resolves), so I don't have to poll the Metrics screen to catch a degraded workload.
requirements.statusDetail: Fixed: closes FUNC-27 -- previously no alerting/notification primitive existed anywhere in the platform; gimle-muninn was a purely passive metrics/logs/traces store with no threshold-evaluation or outbound-notification concept. Added AlertRuleSpec (gimle-mimir manifest: name, optional tenantId, deploymentName, one of five Metric signals matching AutoscalePolicy's own signal set, a GREATER_THAN/LESS_THAN Comparator, threshold, webhookUrl, enabled), Raft-replicated the same way ServiceSpec/NetworkPolicySpec are (StateMutation.PutAlertRule/RemoveAlertRule, StateStore accessors, full StoreRpc/StoreCodec read-path plumbing so a rule created against one control-plane replica is visible on every other). AlertReconciler runs on the same level-triggered reconcile tick as every other reconciler, averaging each enabled rule's configured signal across its deployment's current InstanceObservations (the identical aggregation ApiServer#handleMetrics already uses for the console's own Metrics screen) and calling AlertNotifier#notify exactly once per FIRING/RESOLVED transition -- never re-notifying every tick a condition merely continues to hold. Whether a rule is currently firing is itself now durable, Raft-replicated state (StateMutation.PutAlertFiringState, StateStore#putAlertFiringState/getAlertFiringState) rather than a field kept purely in the reconciler's own process, closing the gap where two control-plane replicas could disagree and a restart silently reset every rule to "not firing"; deleting an AlertRule cascades to clear its durable firing verdict (StateStore#removeAlertRule), so a same-named rule created afterward starts from "never evaluated" rather than inheriting a stale transition. GET /alertrules/{name}/firing (GIMLE-790) serves the verdict, previously nothing did. WebhookAlertNotifier POSTs a small JSON body and is best-effort (an unreachable webhook is logged and dropped, never fails the reconcile tick). ApiServer exposes POST/GET/DELETE /alertrules*, RBAC-gated via the new ResourceKind.ALERT_RULE (tenant view/edit templates include it); gimle-cli gained `get/set/delete alertrule`.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: AlertRuleSpecTest covers constructor validation and the GREATER_THAN/LESS_THAN crossing predicate. AlertReconcilerTest (real StateStore, no mocks) proves: fires once on crossing, never re-fires while still crossed, resolves exactly once when the reading returns to safe, a disabled rule never fires, an unobserved instance contributes nothing to the average (never drags it toward zero), and a deleted rule's durable firing state is cleared rather than leaking forever, an arbitrary starting store with no prior firing history is treated as not-yet-firing, and a freshly instantiated AlertReconciler over the same durable store (standing in for a control-plane restart or failover) reads the already-firing verdict back rather than re-notifying. ApiServerAlertRulesTest covers POST/GET/DELETE/list round-tripping, the enabled flag, 400s on a missing name or blank webhookUrl, replace-on-repost, and cross-replica visibility through one shared store (mirroring ApiServerNetworkPoliciesTest's own proof). RaftCodecTest and StoreCodecTest gained round-trip coverage for the new StateMutation/StoreRpc/StateSnapshot wire shapes. StateStoreTest covers putAlertFiringState/getAlertFiringState round-tripping (absent, true, false), the removeAlertRule cascade, and snapshot round-trip. RaftCodecTest and StoreCodecTest gained round-trip coverage for the new PutAlertFiringState mutation and GetAlertFiringState/AlertFiringStateResult wire shapes.
gherkinSteps: Given an enabled AlertRule on deployment 'checkout-service' with metric=ERROR_RATE_PER_SECOND, comparator=GREATER_THAN, threshold=5.0; When the deployment's averaged observed error rate rises to 8.0 on a reconcile tick; Then exactly one FIRING webhook notification is sent.
Given the rule from the previous scenario is already firing; When a later reconcile tick observes the error rate still above threshold; Then no additional notification is sent.
Given the rule is firing; When the observed error rate drops back to 1.0; Then exactly one RESOLVED webhook notification is sent, and no further notification is sent while it stays resolved.
Given a disabled AlertRule whose metric is currently crossed; When the reconciler evaluates it; Then no notification is ever sent.

requirements.feature: WorkerMetrics evicts a module's Micrometer meters on uninstall, so repeated redeploy no longer accumulates one permanent meter set per (module, version) forever
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator, I want a worker JVM's meter registry to stop growing without bound as modules are redeployed across many versions over the worker's lifetime, so long-running workers don't slowly accumulate stale per-version metrics that were never cleaned up.
requirements.statusDetail: Fixed: closes FUNC-45 -- WorkerMetrics/TaggedRequestMetrics registered a request-count/error-count/latency-timer triple plus thread-count/metaspace gauges per (module, version) tag set and never removed them, so a worker that redeployed the same module name across many versions (or the same version repeatedly) accumulated one permanent meter set per historical (module, version) pair for the worker's entire process lifetime. TaggedRequestMetrics gained evict(Tags), removing its own timer/counter/error-counter triple via MeterRegistry#remove; WorkerMetrics gained evict(ModuleId), removing that triple plus both gauges and clearing the internal gauge-holder cache entry (so a later recordThreadCount/recordMetaspaceBytes for a reused ModuleId re-registers a fresh gauge rather than silently updating an already-removed one). WorkerMain's UninstallModule handler now calls workerMetrics.evict(id) after a successful uninstall (never on a mere stop, since a stopped-but-installed module can restart and resume its counters) -- gated inside the same runCommand lambda so a failed uninstall never evicts. Client-side (fabric outbound-call) metrics are untouched by eviction since they're tagged by callee interface name, not ModuleId.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: WorkerMetricsTest gained evict_removes_every_meter_recorded_for_the_module, evict_does_not_affect_a_different_modules_meters, evict_after_a_second_recording_lets_the_gauge_be_recreated (proving the gauge-holder cache is actually cleared, not merely the registry-side meter), and evict_never_touches_client_side_metrics_which_are_tagged_by_interface_not_module.
gherkinSteps: Given a worker has recorded requests, thread counts, and metaspace bytes for module 'orders@1.0.0'; When that module is successfully uninstalled; Then every meter WorkerMetrics registered for it is removed from the registry.

Given the same module is later reinstalled and recordThreadCount is called again; When its gauge is queried; Then a fresh gauge reflects the new value rather than a stale, already-removed one silently failing to update.
Given two modules 'orders@1.0.0' and 'catalog@1.0.0' both have recorded metrics; When 'orders@1.0.0' is uninstalled and evicted; Then 'catalog@1.0.0''s own meters are untouched.

requirements.feature: Job and CronJob console screens gain a create form, closing the console-only creation gap that previously forced apply -f as the only way to create either kind
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator using the console, I want to create a Job or CronJob directly from the Jobs/CronJobs screens, the same way Deployments already support, so I don't have to drop to the CLI just to submit a run-to-completion or scheduled workload.
requirements.statusDetail: Fixed: closes FUNC-49 -- the Jobs and CronJobs list screens carried a stale comment claiming apply -f was "the supported creation path for now," even though JobsRepository/CronJobsRepository, both Mock and Http implementations, and both Zustand stores already had a working create(spec) with no UI to reach it. Added routes/jobs.new.tsx and routes/cronjobs.new.tsx (mirroring deployments.new.tsx's form/validation/submit pattern) with a "New job"/"New cronjob" button wired into each list screen's header, replacing the stale comments. CronJob's form builds a nested jobTemplate at submit time from flat fields and validates the schedule as exactly five whitespace-separated cron fields via an exported isValidCronSchedule helper. Also fixed a latent bug the new forms would otherwise have hit: HttpJobsRepository/HttpCronJobsRepository's toManifestYaml helpers emitted artifactPath: "" unconditionally instead of omitting it for a blank (registry-resolved) path the way HttpDeploymentsRepository already does, which would have 400'd against ManifestFields.optionalArtifactPath's blank-rejection the moment a user left the artifact path blank to resolve from Andvari.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: New -jobs-new.test.ts/-cronjobs-new.test.ts unit test the exported buildJobSpec/buildCronJobSpec/jobFormIsValid/cronJobFormIsValid/isValidCronSchedule helpers (required-field checks, optional-field omission, tenant NONE-sentinel resolution, backoffLimit clamping, 5-field schedule validation). http/jobs.test.ts and http/cronjobs.test.ts each gained a case asserting a blank artifactPath is omitted from the emitted YAML manifest rather than sent as an empty string.
gherkinSteps: Given the Jobs list screen; When the operator clicks "New job" and submits a valid name/module/version/backoffLimit; Then a JobSpec is created and the operator is navigated to its detail page.

Given the CronJobs list screen; When the operator enters a schedule that is not exactly five whitespace-separated fields; Then submission is rejected with a schedule-format error before any request is sent.
Given a create form with the artifact path left blank; When the spec is submitted; Then the emitted manifest omits the artifactPath key entirely rather than sending an empty string.

requirements.feature: Deployment/DaemonSet/StatefulSet detail pages gain a revision-history panel with rollback, exposing the already-real ControllerRevision/rollback API that previously had no console surface at all
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator, I want to see a workload's revision history and roll it back from its console detail page, the same way I already can from the CLI, so I don't have to leave the console to recover from a bad rollout.
requirements.statusDetail: Fixed: closes FUNC-06 -- GET .../revisions and POST .../rollback were real, CLI-covered APIs for Deployment/DaemonSet/StatefulSet with zero console surface: no type, no repository member, no store method, no UI. Added a shared ControllerRevision type and a new RevisionHistoryPanel component (src/components/revision-history.tsx) rendering a newest-first table with a per-row "Roll back" action behind an AlertDialog confirm, reused identically across all three workload detail routes. Extended DeploymentsRepository/DaemonSetsRepository/StatefulSetsRepository with fetchRevisions/rollback on both Mock (fixture-backed, lazily materializing a synthetic revision 1 and appending forward-only rollback revisions, mirroring the server's own resolveRollbackTarget default-to-previous-revision semantics) and Http implementations (GET .../revisions unwrapping the {revisions:[...]} envelope, POST .../rollback with an optional {toRevision} body), and added loadRevisions/rollback to all three Zustand stores.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: http/{deployments,daemonsets,statefulsets}.test.ts each gained fetchRevisions (URL, envelope unwrap) and rollback (URL, method, {toRevision} body, no-toRevision empty-body default) cases. useDeploymentsStore.test.ts gained loadRevisions/rollback success and error-surfacing cases, including that a successful rollback both updates the item's moduleId in place and refreshes the revision list.
gherkinSteps: Given a deployment's revision history is loaded; When the operator confirms "Roll back" on an older revision; Then a new revision is appended matching that revision's module, and both the deployment and its revision list refresh to reflect it.
Given the revision history table; Then it renders newest-first with the current (index 0) revision showing no rollback action.
Given a rollback request fails server-side; When it returns an error; Then the store surfaces it without silently leaving stale state.

requirements.feature: Node detail/list screens gain cordon/uncordon and taint/untaint controls, exposing the already-real node-scheduling API that previously had no console surface (and whose already-served cordoned/taints fields were silently discarded on the wire)
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator, I want to cordon a node or taint it against a tenant directly from its console detail page, the same way I already can from the CLI, so I don't have to leave the console to take a node out of scheduling rotation.
requirements.statusDetail: Fixed: closes FUNC-07 -- POST /nodes/{id}/{cordon|uncordon} and POST /nodes/{id}/{taint|untaint} were real, CLI-covered, idempotent, future-scheduling-only APIs (never evicting a running instance), and GET /nodes already served cordoned/taints per node -- but the console's own RawNode/mapNode silently discarded both fields, and the node detail page's only actions were Back and View logs. Extended the Node type with cordoned/taints, fixed HttpNodesRepository's mapNode to stop discarding them, added setCordoned/setTaint to NodesRepository (Mock mutating the fixture in place; Http issuing the same empty-body POST the CLI's own cordon/uncordon calls make, and a {tenantId}-bodied POST for taint/untaint) and to useNodesStore. The node detail page gained a Cordon/Uncordon button behind an AlertDialog confirm plus a cordoned status badge, and a Taints panel listing current taints with a per-taint remove action and a tenant picker to add one; the node list screen gained a cordoned badge alongside the existing stale/healthy status.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: http/nodes.test.ts gained cordoned/taints wire-normalization cases (defaulted and real-value) plus setCordoned/setTaint URL/method/body cases. New useNodesStore.test.ts covers setCordoned/setTaint success (item mutated in place, taint set sorted and de-duplicated) and repository-rejection error surfacing.
gherkinSteps: Given a node's detail page; When the operator confirms "Cordon"; Then the node is marked cordoned and a cordoned badge appears, with no running instance evicted.
Given a cordoned node; When the operator adds a taint for a tenant; Then that tenant is added to the node's taint set, sorted and without duplicating an already-present entry.
Given the node list screen; Then a cordoned node shows a cordoned badge alongside its stale/healthy status.

requirements.feature: GET /tenants and /tenants/{id} expose real, server-computed usage (memoryBytes/cpuMillicores/instances) and a quotaViolating flag, closing the gap where the console's Tenants screens could show only configured limits, never actual consumption
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator, I want to see how much of a tenant's quota is actually in use, and whether it's currently violating, from the same place I see the quota itself, so I don't have to cross-reference QuotaReconciler logs or admission rejections to understand a tenant's real headroom.
requirements.statusDetail: Fixed: closes FUNC-50 -- TenantUsage.currentlyAssigned already computed real per-tenant memory/CPU/instance consumption (resourceRequest x committedInstances summed across every Deployment/Job/DaemonSet/StatefulSet sharing the tenant) but was consulted only internally, at admission (TenantQuotaPlugin) and by QuotaReconciler; GET /tenants/{id} returned only {id, quota}. ApiServer.tenantToJson is now an instance method (was static) that additionally computes usage via the same TenantUsage.currentlyAssigned call admission and QuotaReconciler already use -- not a separately-derived approximation -- and adds {usage: {memoryBytes, cpuMillicores, instances}, quotaViolating: boolean} to both the list and single-tenant response. The console's Tenant type, HttpTenantsRepository (updateQuota now re-fetches after a PUT since a changed quota can flip quotaViolating even though usage is unchanged), fixture mock data, and both Tenants screens were updated to consume and render it: the list screen shows used/max per resource plus a quota-status badge, and the detail screen gained a 'Quota usage' panel using a Bullet gauge component lifted out of metrics.tsx (its only prior consumer) into a shared src/components/usage-bullet.tsx so both screens render the identical gauge style.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: ApiServerConsoleContractTest.tenant_has_every_field_the_console_needs extended to assert usage.memoryBytes/cpuMillicores/instances and quotaViolating are present. ApiServerTest.deployment_submission_within_tenant_quota_succeeds extended to assert real usage numbers (16Mi/10m/1 instance, matching TestModuleBuilder.minimalDescriptor's fixed request) after a real deployment submission. Console: repositories/http/tenants.test.ts's updateQuota case rewritten to assert the PUT-then-GET re-fetch and that a changed quotaViolating is picked up.
gherkinSteps: Given a tenant with one deployment committing 16Mi memory and 10m cpu; When its tenant record is fetched; Then usage.memoryBytes/cpuMillicores/instances reflect exactly that committed usage, the same numbers admission and QuotaReconciler enforce against.

Given a tenant whose usage already exceeds a smaller quota; When its quota is updated to that smaller value; Then quotaViolating becomes true on the very next fetch, not left stale from before the update.
Given the Tenants list screen; Then each row shows used/max for memory, cpu, and instances plus a quota-status badge, not configured limits alone.

requirements.feature: apply -f now covers Service, NetworkPolicy, Tenant, LimitRange, Role, RoleBinding, and Account manifests, closing the gap where these seven kinds needed their own bespoke gimle set <kind> flag-based command and had no manifest-driven creation path at all
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator scripting or version-controlling cluster configuration, I want apply -f to work for every resource kind the same way it works for Deployment/Job/CronJob/DaemonSet/StatefulSet, so I'm not forced into a second, flag-based command with its own divergent syntax for RBAC, networking, and tenant resources.
requirements.statusDetail: Fixed: closes FUNC-32 -- apply -f's kind: dispatch previously covered only Deployment/Job/CronJob/DaemonSet/StatefulSet/ArtifactSet/KindDefinition, falling through to the generic custom-resource PUT (and a confusing server-side 400) for Service/NetworkPolicy/Tenant/LimitRange/Role/RoleBinding/Account, each of which instead needed its own gimle set <kind> ... flag-heavy command. Unlike the workload kinds, none of these seven has a PUT /{kind}/{name}-shaped route to send manifest YAML to directly (ServicesCommand/NetworkPolicyCommand POST a JSON body to a bare collection; TenantsCommand/LimitRangeCommand/RolesCommand/RoleBindingsCommand/AccountsCommand PUT JSON built from CLI flags) -- so each command gained its own apply(args, err) that parses the manifest client-side via a new ManifestFiles.parseRoot(file, bytes) (returning the whole YAML root as a Map, alongside the existing single-field extractName/extractKind) and builds the identical JSON body its own set already builds from flags, then issues the same request set would. GimleCli.handleApply's kind: switch now routes all seven. Tenant/LimitRange/RoleBinding/Account manifests use name: for the identifier, matching every other kind's own top-level field, even though those four commands' get/set/delete verbs call it id or username.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: GimleCliTest gained one apply_<kind>_then_get_<kind>_round_trips test per new kind (Service, NetworkPolicy including its no-direction-restricted client-side rejection, Tenant, LimitRange, Role, RoleBinding, Account with groups), each writing a manifest, applying it, and asserting the resulting resource via a real GET against a real ApiServer -- the same real-server convention every existing GimleCliTest case uses.
gherkinSteps: Given a Service manifest naming a deploymentNames list and a port; When it is applied via apply -f; Then GET service <name> returns the same deploymentNames/port/targetPort a set service call with equivalent flags would have produced.

Given a NetworkPolicy manifest with neither allowedCallerTenantIds nor allowedCalleeTenantIds declared; When it is applied; Then the CLI rejects it client-side before any request is sent, the same restrict-at-least-one-direction rule set networkpolicy enforces.

Given a Role manifest listing lowercase resource/verb permission entries; When applied and then read back; Then each permission's resource/verb is stored uppercased, matching set role's own normalization.

requirements.feature: gimle get <workload-kind> <name> -o manifest projects the status response back into a re-appliable manifest, and apply -f - reads a manifest from stdin, closing the round-trip gap where get's own output could never be fed back into apply
requirements.userStory: As a platform operator, I want to read a live workload's manifest back out, tweak one field, and reapply it, so recovering or adjusting a running deployment doesn't require hand-reconstructing its manifest from scratch or reverse-engineering the status JSON's nested shape.
requirements.statusDetail: Fixed: closes FUNC-65 -- every apply-capable workload kind's manifest requires a top-level module: key, but gimle get <kind> <name>'s response renamed that same reference to moduleId and nested it three levels down (status -> spec -> moduleId) alongside read-only fields (instances, unplacedCount, quotaViolating, ...) no parser accepts -- so 'read a live resource back out, tweak one field, reapply it' always failed with a missing-field error, and apply -f had no stdin support for piping a generated manifest in directly. Added OutputFormat.Kind.MANIFEST (-o manifest, honored only by get <deployment|job|cronjob|daemonset|statefulset> <name>) backed by a new ManifestExport class that rebuilds kind:/name:/module: at the manifest root per kind, omits a blank artifactPath entirely (a present-but-blank one is a manifest error -- ManifestFields.optionalArtifactPath), maps autoscale's wire combinationMode (WORST_SIGNAL/WEIGHTED) back to the manifest's own mode: (worst-signal/weighted) key, and drops every status-only field. Separately, -f - now reads the manifest from stdin (kubectl's own convention): ManifestFiles.readManifestBytes memoizes stdin's single read for the duration of one apply invocation (each resource-specific command's own apply independently re-reads the manifest for its own name: extraction after GimleCli.handleApply's own kind: peek, which would otherwise drain stdin on the first read and starve the second), and GimleCli.handleApply resets that memoized cache at the start of every invocation so an unrelated later apply -f - call never sees stale bytes from an earlier one.
sourceLocations: `gimle-cli/src/main/java/com/gimle/cli/GimleCli.java` (`handleApply` resets the stdin cache; `-o manifest` accepted by `parseOutputKind`)
requirements.testCoverageDetail: GimleCliTest.get_deployment_as_manifest_then_reapplying_it_round_trips: applies a deployment, exports it via -o manifest, asserts the exported YAML contains kind:/name:/module:/replicas: and excludes moduleId/instances, then reapplies the exported file and asserts success -- the actual round trip the bug report described. GimleCliTest.apply_dash_f_dash_reads_the_manifest_from_stdin: redirects System.in to a manifest and asserts apply -f - succeeds and the resulting deployment is visible via a normal GET.
gherkinSteps: Given a deployment created via apply -f; When its manifest is exported via get deployment <name> -o manifest; Then the output contains a top-level module: block (not moduleId) and no status-only fields.
Given that exported manifest saved to a file; When it is applied via apply -f unchanged; Then the apply succeeds -- the full round trip that previously failed with a missing-field error.
Given a manifest piped to stdin; When applied via apply -f -; Then the resulting resource is created exactly as it would be from an equivalent file, with no second, empty read draining the stream.

requirements.feature: Fabric calls retry only where retrying is provably safe, with server-side correlationId deduplication
requirements.userStory: As a module author, I want the platform to retry a failed cross-worker service call only when retrying cannot duplicate an effect, so that a transport failure does not silently apply my non-idempotent mutation twice.
requirements.statusDetail: Fixed: closes FUNC-33. FabricClient.call opened one connection, sent one request, and either returned or threw -- no retry anywhere -- while correlationId rode the wire frame purely to satisfy the sealed-interface shape and was never used for deduplication. A caller whose target died mid-call got an exception with no guidance on whether retrying was safe. Now a failure raised before the connection is established is wrapped as FabricConnectException and fails over to a different endpoint through the existing tier/version/breaker selection path whatever the method does (nothing ran, so nothing can duplicate); a failure after the request was written is retried only when the target method carries the new @Idempotent annotation, matched by annotation-type name so a module layer's own copy still counts. Attempts of one logical call share a correlationId, and FabricServer routes every inbound request through a bounded (4096), time-windowed (60s) InvocationDeduplicator that replays an already-answered id's response (InvokeError included) rather than re-executing, makes a duplicate arriving mid-flight wait on the original rather than race it, and deliberately does not remember an id whose dispatch threw. Bounded at MAX_CALL_ATTEMPTS=3; invokeByName has no resolved Method and is never retried past the write.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: InvocationDeduplicatorTest, FabricServerDeduplicationTest, FabricServiceRegistryRetryTest (+ RetryableGreeter fixture), FabricClientTest connect-time vs mid-call classification. FabricServiceRegistryTest's spillover test was changed from a refused port to an accept-then-hang-up endpoint so it still exercises a mid-call failure rather than being satisfied by the new connect-time failover.
gherkinSteps: Given a service method not annotated @Idempotent
When the call fails after the request was written
Then the failure is surfaced to the caller rather than retried
And when the connection was never established, the call fails over to a different endpoint
And a duplicate correlationId replays the original response instead of executing twice

requirements.feature: Per-endpoint circuit breaker state is visible as logs and shipped Micrometer meters
requirements.userStory: As an operator debugging why traffic is not reaching an instance, I want to see whether a per-endpoint circuit breaker is the cause, so that I can distinguish an open breaker from an unknown endpoint or an unready instance.
requirements.statusDetail: Fixed: closes FUNC-78. CircuitBreaker.state() was called from nowhere outside the breaker's own transition logic -- no metric, API field or console indicator anywhere -- and the only externally visible trace of a trip was a single log line in the cluster-wide panic-mode branch, so an individual endpoint's breaker opening produced no log, metric or queryable state at all. CircuitBreaker gained a TransitionListener (notified outside its own lock, so a slow listener cannot stall a call path), FabricServiceRegistry logs every transition (WARN on open, INFO on half-open/close, naming the callee interface and nodeId/workerId), and WorkerMetrics registers gimle.fabric.circuitbreaker.state (gauge: 0 CLOSED, 1 HALF_OPEN, 2 OPEN) and gimle.fabric.circuitbreaker.transitions (counter tagged by state entered). Both ride the existing MeterSnapshotCodec -> agent -> Muninn path and are queryable through /metrics-history/*, so no new ControlMessage or heartbeat field was needed. Initial CLOSED state is published on breaker creation and meters are evicted when a breaker leaves the bounded per-endpoint map.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: CircuitBreakerTest (four listener tests: full open/half-open/close cycle, no-op calls report nothing, cooldown expiry seen only by a candidacy check still reported, failed half-open trial reports the re-open); FabricServiceRegistryRetryTest asserts the gauge level, the transition counter and the logged line via a Logback ListAppender.
gherkinSteps: Given a fabric endpoint whose calls are failing
When its circuit breaker opens
Then a WARN line names the interface and the nodeId/workerId endpoint
And gimle.fabric.circuitbreaker.state reports 2 for that endpoint
And the transition counter increments for the state entered

requirements.feature: Cluster DNS answers NODATA, not NXDOMAIN, for a declared Service with no live endpoints
requirements.userStory: As an operator debugging name resolution during a rollout, I want a Service that exists but currently has no endpoints to answer NOERROR with zero records, so that a deploy in flight is never indistinguishable from a typo'd or never-declared name.
requirements.statusDetail: Fixed: closes FUNC-11. ControlPlaneServicePoller filtered a Service out of the cache entirely whenever its endpoint list was empty (.filter(endpoints -> !endpoints.endpoints().isEmpty())), so a Service mid-rollout or scaled to zero -- which ServiceReconciler's own javadoc calls a normal, valid outcome -- returned NXDOMAIN, contradicting SkaldServer's own javadoc preferring NOERROR/zero-answers for exactly this case. ServiceDirectory.resolveAll now returns Optional<List<HostPort>> so the two states are expressible at all: absent means no such name, present-but-empty means known Service with zero endpoints. The poller keeps empty Services; only a per-service 404 (the Service vanished between the catalog listing and the fetch) still drops a name. SkaldServer answers NXDOMAIN for an unknown name, NOERROR with zero answers for a known-and-empty one for both A and SRV queries, and SERVFAIL when the cached data is severely stale -- the zero-endpoint case included, since 'no endpoints' is itself a claim about current cluster state. A dashed per-endpoint name under an empty Service stays NXDOMAIN, which is correct: that specific name genuinely does not exist.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: SkaldServerTest (5 new: known-empty answers NOERROR for A and for SRV, unknown stays NXDOMAIN alongside a known-empty one, dashed endpoint name under an empty Service stays NXDOMAIN, severely stale empty is SERVFAIL); ControlPlaneServicePollerTest (a_service_with_no_endpoints_stays_in_the_cache_as_a_known_empty_name replaces the old test that asserted the defect); CachingServiceDirectoryTest (absent vs present-but-empty, and a refresh that empties a name keeps it known).
gherkinSteps: Given a declared Service whose backing deployment is scaled to zero
When a client resolves that Service name
Then the responder answers NOERROR with zero answer records
And a name that was never declared still answers NXDOMAIN

requirements.feature: Gateway TLS selects a per-virtual-host certificate from the client's SNI extension
requirements.userStory: As an operator running one TLS-terminating gateway in front of several hostnames, I want each hostname to present its own certificate, so that every routed host passes a client's hostname verification rather than only whichever host the single configured certificate covered.
requirements.statusDetail: Fixed: closes FUNC-52. TLS termination built one HttpsServer from a single SslContexts.forMutualTls(...) call at startup with no per-connection certificate selection, even though GatewayRouteConfig implements virtual hosting ([HOST <hostname>] route lines) and dispatch genuinely routes by the inbound Host header -- so with TLS on and more than one hostname routed, every host except the one the configured certificate's SAN covered failed validation for any client that checks hostnames. A new optional gateway.tlsCertificates config binds <hostname> <certFile> <keyFile> per line (same line/comment shape as gateway.routes), and a custom X509ExtendedKeyManager reads ExtendedSSLSession#getRequestedServerNames in chooseServerAlias/chooseEngineServerAlias to present the right certificate per connection. No SNIMatcher is installed, deliberately: a matcher refuses an unrecognized hostname, which would take host-unconstrained fallback routes down with it -- a client sending no SNI, and one naming an unbound hostname, both fall back to the cluster-wide certificate. The JSSE plumbing lives in gimle-core's existing com.gimle.core.tls as an overload whose empty-list case delegates to the existing single-certificate method, so the degenerate case is literally the previous code path.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: GatewayTlsConfigTest and GatewayHooksTlsTest (11 new): per-host certificate presented for each SNI name, no-SNI falls back to the cluster-wide certificate, an unbound hostname falls back rather than failing the handshake, wildcards/duplicate hostnames/wrong field counts/missing files rejected at parse time.
gherkinSteps: Given a gateway terminating TLS for two routed hostnames
When a client connects with SNI naming the second hostname
Then the gateway presents that hostname's own certificate
And a client sending no SNI receives the cluster-wide certificate

requirements.feature: Autoscale policies carry scale-up and scale-down stabilization windows backed by durable last-scale state
requirements.userStory: As an operator tuning autoscaling under real noisy metrics, I want separate scale-up and scale-down stabilization windows, so that a metric oscillating around its target cannot scale a deployment up and back down on consecutive reconcile ticks.
requirements.statusDetail: Fixed: closes FUNC-10. Scale-up/down and multiple trigger metrics with combination modes were genuinely implemented, but no cooldown/stabilization field existed anywhere in the policy and AutoscaleReconciler adjusted by exactly +/-1 replica every tick off that tick's signal alone, with no 'time since last scale event' check in the class -- so a metric oscillating around its threshold could scale up, then down, then up indefinitely. AutoscalePolicy gained scaleUpCooldown and scaleDownCooldown Durations, defaulting asymmetrically the way operators expect (DEFAULT_SCALE_UP_COOLDOWN 0, so a load spike is answered on the next tick; DEFAULT_SCALE_DOWN_COOLDOWN 5 minutes, matching HPA's own scale-down stabilization default); explicit 0 disables a window and a negative value is rejected. Critically the 'time since last scale' is durable observed state, not a reconciler field: a new deploymentLastScale map in StateStore is written by a new StateMutation.PutDeploymentLastScale riding the same batch as the PutEffectiveReplicas it accounts for, replicated through RaftCodec (mutation and snapshot), readable over StoreRpc.GetDeploymentLastScale, and cleared on removeDeployment so a recreated name does not inherit an old window -- so the window survives a control-plane restart or failover and the reconciler stays level-triggered. Clamping an out-of-range stored replica count back into [minReplicas, maxReplicas] is computed separately from the signal-driven step and is deliberately never suppressed, since that is a bounds correction rather than a scaling decision.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: AutoscaleReconcilerTest (8 new, including the explicit oscillation test proving a scale-up cannot be reversed inside its window, a fresh-reconciler test proving the window is read from durable store state rather than instance state, convergence from a future-dated stamp left by a clock-skewed replica, and out-of-range clamping still applied while the signal step is suppressed); AutoscalePolicyTest, DeploymentManifestParserTest, StateStoreTest, RaftCodecTest, StoreCodecTest, ApiServerTest, ManifestExportTest.
gherkinSteps: Given a deployment with a scale-down stabilization window
When its signal crosses the target and immediately falls back
Then the replica count is not reversed until the window elapses
And the window still applies after the control plane replica restarts

requirements.feature: CronJob schedules can be suspended without deleting and recreating them
requirements.userStory: As an operator handling a maintenance window or a misbehaving schedule, I want to suspend a CronJob, so that it stops firing while keeping its firing history and identity.
requirements.statusDetail: Fixed: closes FUNC-54. CronJobSpec had no suspend/paused field and CronJobReconciler fired every non-terminal CronJob every tick with no pause check anywhere, so the only way to stop a schedule was delete-then-recreate, which cannot preserve prior firing history across the round trip. CronJobSpec gained a suspend boolean (manifest suspend:, default false), parsed, persisted through DomainCodec, surfaced on the API read side and in the CLI. A suspended CronJob records each due instant as it passes but plans no firing, so it keeps its history, stays listed, and unsuspending resumes at the next due instant rather than back-firing every missed schedule -- and it advances at its own schedule's cadence, not the reconcile loop's. History pruning still runs. triggerNow still fires a suspended CronJob, documented as deliberate since kubectl create job --from=cronjob/x behaves the same way.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: CronJobReconcilerTest (5 new: a suspended CronJob never fires from any starting tick; unsuspending resumes at the next due instant without back-firing the backlog; history is preserved across suspend/unsuspend; convergence from an arbitrary mid-schedule state; triggerNow still fires); CronJobManifestParserTest, ManifestExportTest.
gherkinSteps: Given a CronJob with suspend true
When the reconciler ticks past several due instants
Then no Job is generated
And when suspend is set back to false, the next due instant fires exactly once

requirements.feature: Health probe interval, timeout and liveness failure threshold are declarable per module
requirements.userStory: As a module author whose readiness check legitimately needs longer than the worker default, I want to declare my own probe interval, timeout and failure threshold in the manifest, so that a slow but healthy module is not reported as broken on every tick.
requirements.statusDetail: Fixed: closes FUNC-36. Probe interval (1s), timeout (2s) and liveness failure threshold (3) were literal constants applied identically to every module a worker hosts, and the manifest's health: block carried only initialDelaySeconds -- so a module whose readiness check needs more than two seconds (a cold cache fill, a slow downstream dependency) failed every readiness tick indistinguishably from a genuinely broken probe. The health: block gained intervalSeconds, timeoutSeconds and failureThreshold; HealthProbes carries them as Optional<Duration>/OptionalInt with a compact constructor enforcing positive interval and timeout, non-negative initial delay and threshold >= 1; the parser rejects zero, negative and non-numeric values with GimleManifestException. WorkerRuntime.onActive resolves each module's effective timing from its own descriptor with the worker default as fallback and records the effective liveness threshold per module at ACTIVE rather than re-reading it on failure, so a concurrent uninstall cannot strand the lookup. The three worker-wide constants are now explicitly named defaults.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: HealthProbesTest (9 new, every validation failure); ModuleDescriptorParserTest (8 added, including zero/negative/non-numeric for each field); WorkerRuntimeProbeTimingTest (5 new, real dynamically-loaded fixture modules through a real ModuleController/WorkerRuntime: a declared timeoutSeconds keeps a 400ms readiness check ready against a 100ms worker default while the same check without it is cut off; declared vs default failureThreshold; a declared long intervalSeconds suppresses fast-cadence probing).
gherkinSteps: Given a module manifest declaring a probe timeout longer than the worker default
When its readiness check takes longer than the worker default but less than the declared timeout
Then the instance is reported ready
And a manifest declaring a zero or negative interval is rejected at parse time

requirements.feature: Instance event history is cleared when a workload is removed, so a reused name starts clean
requirements.userStory: As an operator reusing a workload name, I want a newly created Deployment, DaemonSet or StatefulSet to show only its own instance events, so that an unrelated predecessor's timeline does not bleed into it.
requirements.statusDetail: Fixed: closes FUNC-37. removeDeployment, removeDaemonSetSpec and removeStatefulSetSpec each explicitly cleared that workload's ControllerRevision history -- with removeDeployment's own javadoc spelling out exactly why a name reuse would otherwise bleed old history into a new, unrelated resource -- but instanceEvents, keyed by the identical (name, index) composite, had no equivalent cleanup anywhere, leaving the exact bug that cleanup was written to prevent live on its sibling structure. All three removal paths now call a private clearInstanceEventsFor(tenantId, name) beside the existing controllerRevisions.remove(...). The helper drops every instanceEvents key under the scoped key plus '#' whose remainder is all digits, so a similarly-named workload (orders vs orders#eu) is untouched. Because the cleanup lives inside the removal method the corresponding StateMutation applies, it rides the replicated Raft path rather than mutating a map behind the log, and the cleared timelines are consequently absent from snapshot() too.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: StateStoreTest (7 new: every index cleared; delete-then-recreate starts empty for all three workload kinds; another tenant's same-named timeline survives; a similarly-named workload survives; a cleared timeline does not return through a snapshot/restore round trip); MutationBatchTest (replaying PutDeployment, AppendInstanceEvent, RemoveDeployment, PutDeployment in log order on a fresh replica leaves the recreated name empty).
gherkinSteps: Given a Deployment with recorded instance events
When it is deleted and an unrelated Deployment is created with the same name
Then the new Deployment's event timeline is empty
And the cleared timeline does not reappear after a snapshot restore or log replay

requirements.feature: RBAC permissions accept a wildcard sentinel in the resource, verb and tenant-scope positions
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want to grant a role breadth without hand-enumerating every resource and verb combination, so that a custom role narrower than cluster-admin but broader than the fixed tenant templates is expressible and stays correct as new resource kinds are added.
requirements.statusDetail: Fixed: closes FUNC-58. No wildcard sentinel was recognized anywhere in com.gimle.core.authz -- --permission "*:read" threw a loud 400 -- and the only breadth mechanism was a fixed set of built-in templates hardcoded in Java source, so a role like 'read every resource kind across every tenant except SECRET' had to be hand-enumerated and re-edited every time a ResourceKind was added. Permission's resource and verb became Optional<ResourceKind>/Optional<Verb>, empty meaning every value -- the same 'absent constraint is unconstrained' semantics tenantScope already had, so all three positions read alike -- with Permission.ALL ("*") as the single written spelling and covers/coversResource/coversVerb doing the widening. The sentinel is persisted as a sentinel and expanded at authorize time, never at write time, so a grant automatically covers a ResourceKind added later without the stored role being rewritten. The qualifier position deliberately rejects the wildcard, so a wildcard resource grant still never reaches a {kind}/status write. Auditing every authorize call site found one parallel matcher: Authorizer.hasAnyReadGrant compared permission.resource()/verb() directly and would have silently denied the collection-list gate to a wildcard holder; it now delegates to the shared matching, so all defense-in-depth re-checkers (gimle-controlplane, gimle-fafnir, gimle-muninn, gimle-andvari, and gimle-agent's admin fault API) behave identically.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: PermissionTest (10 new: wildcard in each position, wildcard combined with a named value, token round-trip, malformed/blank/unknown input, wildcard-qualifier rejection, wildcard never reaching a {kind}/status write); WildcardPermissionAuthzTest (new, 11: every ResourceKind covered by one stored grant, the stored role staying a single unexpanded permission, codec round-trip preserving the wildcard, a narrower grant alongside a wildcard grant, hasAnyReadGrant, an unbound principal unaffected); GimleCliTest (3 added).
gherkinSteps: Given a role granting the wildcard resource with the read verb
When a bound subject reads two different resource kinds
Then both reads are allowed
And a write is still refused
And the stored role remains a single unexpanded permission

requirements.feature: Overlapping Services are announced with a response warning rather than silently allowed
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want to be told when a Service I create fronts a Deployment another Service already fronts, so that a copy-paste mistake is visible while an intentional shared front door stays possible.
requirements.statusDetail: Fixed: closes FUNC-34. Nothing checked a new ServiceSpec against any other Service's deploymentNames -- not the constructor, not ServiceRegistry.put, not the API handler -- so two Services naming the same Deployment each got their own live, correct-looking endpoint list pointed at the same instances, with nothing distinguishing an intentional shared front door from a typo and no console or CLI warning either. Because a shared front door is a legitimate pattern, this warns rather than rejects: the create still succeeds, and the control plane attaches an X-Gimle-Warning header naming each overlapping Service and the deployment names actually shared, which gimle set service and gimle apply -f print as a warning: line on stderr. No force or confirm flag was added.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: ServiceAdvisoriesTest (overlap reported; one warning per overlapping Service, name-ordered; a self re-submit does not overlap itself; the same deployment name under a different tenant is not an overlap; disjoint names earn nothing); ApiServerServicesTest (4 tests); GimleCliTest asserts the warning reaches stderr without failing the command.
gherkinSteps: Given a Service fronting a deployment
When a second Service is declared fronting the same deployment
Then the create succeeds
And the response carries a warning naming the first Service and the shared deployment

requirements.feature: A Service's targetPort is authoritative when declared and genuinely absent when not
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want a Service's targetPort to decide which port traffic actually reaches, so that the field is not a silent no-op on a multi-port instance or a silent traffic-dropper when nothing reports it.
requirements.statusDetail: Fixed: closes FUNC-53. targetPort was validated only for numeric range at admission and never against what any backing instance reported, and at resolution time ServiceEndpointResolver.resolve never read spec.targetPort() for the deployment-selector case at all -- solePort instead required the instance to report exactly one declared port and used it verbatim. So an operator could create a Service naming a targetPort no instance reports with no admission error, and the field had zero effect for any deployment reporting more than one port. targetPort is now OptionalInt and authoritative when declared: each backing instance contributes an endpoint on exactly that port, and an instance not reporting it is excluded with a logged reason (deduplicated per Service so a seconds-long tick does not spam) rather than quietly contributing a different port. Omitted, it is genuinely absent rather than defaulted to port: an instance reporting exactly one port contributes it, one reporting zero or several contributes nothing. Because instance ports are reported at runtime through ModuleContext.reportPort, a targetPort no instance currently reports cannot be a hard admission error -- it is level-triggered state -- so it is admitted with an X-Gimle-Warning instead. DomainCodec encodes 0 as undeclared, leaving the wire shape unchanged at one int.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: ServiceReconcilerTest (declared targetPort selects out of a multi-port instance; an instance not reporting it is excluded; no targetPort with exactly one reported port resolves; no targetPort with several stays ambiguous; a targetPort appearing and disappearing converges both ways; repeated ticks over an unchanged store keep producing the same endpoints); ApiServerServicesTest (5); ServiceAdvisoriesTest; ServiceSpecTest; GimleCliTest; console services repository tests.
gherkinSteps: Given a deployment whose instance reports two ports
When a Service is declared fronting it with the second port as targetPort
Then the Service resolves exactly one endpoint on that port
And a Service declaring a port no instance reports resolves no endpoints and was warned about at creation

requirements.feature: NetworkPolicy edits are version-guarded and can add or remove one allow-list entry at a time
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want to add or remove a single caller tenant on an existing NetworkPolicy under a version guard, so that a concurrent edit is refused rather than silently overwritten and a client reconstructing the spec cannot accidentally un-scope the policy.
requirements.statusDetail: Fixed: closes FUNC-12. NetworkPolicyRegistry exposed only whole-object put/get/list/remove -- no PATCH, no expectedVersion guard, unlike the sibling ConfigMap API's lease-guarded read-check-propose path -- and gimle set networkpolicy replaced the whole rule set too, so adding or removing one caller tenant meant GET-reconstruct-POST of the entire spec client-side: a lost-update race under any concurrent edit, and a client that omitted a field while reconstructing silently un-scoped the policy. The registry now follows the existing ConfigMap lease-guarded read-check-propose pattern rather than a new idiom, every write carries an expectedVersion guard that refuses a stale edit with 409, and the CLI gained --add-/--remove-allowed-caller-tenant and --add-/--remove-allowed-callee-tenant which read, amend and write under that guard.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: NetworkPolicyRegistryTest (the actual lost-update race, not just the happy path), ApiServerNetworkPoliciesTest, GimleCliTest.
gherkinSteps: Given a network policy allowing one caller tenant
When a second caller tenant is added through the amend flag
And a concurrent edit is attempted against the version it started from
Then the concurrent edit is rejected with status 409
And both amendments are visible through a different control-plane replica

requirements.feature: A NetworkPolicy may only name tenants that exist
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want a policy naming a tenant that does not exist to be refused at admission, so that a typo does not become a permanently dangling rule I never get feedback about.
requirements.statusDetail: Fixed: closes FUNC-35. NetworkPolicySpec's compact constructor validated the blankness and shape of allowedCallerTenantIds/allowedCalleeTenantIds but never checked any listed tenant ID against a real tenant registry, and neither did the registry's put nor the API handler -- so a typo'd or since-deleted tenant ID was silently accepted as a permanently-unreachable or dangling rule. Existence is now checked at admission in the API handler, which is the only layer that can reach a tenant registry; the record's compact constructor stays a pure shape check, since a record cannot and should not reach a registry.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: ApiServerNetworkPoliciesTest; GimleCliTest's networkpolicy round-trip tests now declare the tenants their policies name.
gherkinSteps: Given a cluster with no tenant named partner
When a network policy allowing caller tenant partner is created
Then the create is rejected with status 400 naming the unknown tenant

requirements.feature: A tenant can be closed to cross-tenant fabric calls before its first NetworkPolicy exists
requirements.userStory: As an operator provisioning a new tenant, I want to declare it deny-by-default immediately, so that it is not fully open to cross-tenant calls for however long it takes to author its first policy.
requirements.statusDetail: Fixed: closes FUNC-77. Every enforcement check consulted only the current, possibly-empty networkPolicies list, so an empty list -- every brand-new tenant's starting state -- meant the check loop never ran and nothing was ever denied. That matches the documented deny-by-default-once-a-policy-exists design exactly; the gap was that no per-tenant posture flag or deny-all shorthand existed to flip a new tenant closed beforehand. Tenant gained an isolationPosture of OPEN (the default, so existing behavior is unchanged unless an operator opts in) or DENY_BY_DEFAULT, under which an empty policy set denies rather than permits. It is set through gimle set tenant --isolation-posture, relayed to every worker on the same NetworkPolicyRelay -> ControlMessage.NetworkPoliciesUpdated path the policies themselves ride (via a new denyByDefaultTenantIds field and a new /networkpostures endpoint the agent polls), and re-checked independently by FabricServer. BifrostProxy consumes it too, keeping its documented fail-closed posture coherent for a deny-by-default tenant.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: ControlMessageCodecTest, NetworkPolicyRelayTest, HttpNetworkPolicySourceTest (including a test asserting only tenants declaring deny-by-default are reported closed), BifrostProxyTest, FabricServerTest.
gherkinSteps: Given a tenant declared DENY_BY_DEFAULT with no network policies
When another tenant calls one of its services over the fabric
Then the call is refused
And the same call against an OPEN tenant with no policies succeeds

requirements.feature: Every secret version records who wrote it, when, and its declared type
requirements.userStory: As an incident reviewer, I want to know who wrote version N of a secret and when, so that I do not have to correlate a bare version list against a cluster-wide audit ring buffer by eyeballing timestamps.
requirements.statusDetail: Fixed: closes FUNC-19. secret versions returned bare version integers only -- neither the Meta pointer record nor the underlying ConfigEntry carried a timestamp or author -- and while the audit trail captured principal and timestamp at write time it never captured the resulting version number, with GET /audit offering no key filter. Each version now records the writing principal, the wall-clock write time and its declared type on the key@meta pointer's append-only versions list, returned by the version listing and by a single-key read; the write's own audit event now carries the version it produced, via a new append-only OptionalInt version field on AuditEvent encoded at the end of DomainCodec's existing encoding with no format-version constant bumped.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: SecretStoreTest (author and timestamp on every version; soft delete and undelete leave write history intact; versionInfo for a missing version is empty); FafnirServerTest; AuditEventTest (a versioned write carries its version; an unversioned resource kind carries none; a null version coalesces to empty); SecretCommandTest; console repository and store tests.
gherkinSteps: Given a secret written by a known principal
When its version list is read
Then each version reports its author, write time and type
And the audit event for that write carries the version it produced

requirements.feature: A secret write may declare its value's shape, validated before anything is stored
requirements.userStory: As an operator storing TLS material, I want a malformed PEM rejected at the secret set call, so that the failure surfaces where it was caused rather than much later when a module tries to parse it at launch.
requirements.statusDetail: Fixed: closes FUNC-60. validateKey checked only the key name; the plaintext value was encrypted and stored completely unexamined, and no secret type concept existed anywhere in the platform, so a value a manifest would later mount as a TLS key or certificate was accepted with no shape validation at write time. A write may now declare a type -- opaque (the default, and the only unvalidated one), pem-certificate, or pem-private-key -- validated structurally before anything is encrypted or stored, with the type persisted per version and reported on read. The private-key type accepts every openssl-emitted label (PKCS#8, PKCS#1, SEC1, encrypted), since rejecting a valid key purely for its label would make the type useless for real material. The CLI gained --type and --from-file, the latter because a multi-line PEM cannot otherwise be supplied.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: SecretTypeTest (new, 12: wire-name parsing, opaque accepts anything, missing/truncated/empty-body/non-base64 PEM rejection, every openssl private-key label accepted, mismatched begin/end labels rejected, a certificate refused where a private key was declared); SecretStoreTest (4); FafnirServerTest (malformed rejected with 400 and never stored; unknown type rejected); SecretCommandTest (3); console tests.
gherkinSteps: Given a secret write declaring the pem-certificate type
When the value is a truncated PEM
Then the write is rejected and nothing is stored
And a well-formed value is stored with its type reported on read

requirements.feature: A tenant's whole secret set can be exported and imported in one authorized, audited call
requirements.userStory: As an operator migrating a tenant to a freshly bootstrapped cluster with a new master key, I want a supported bulk export and import, so that I do not have to script a per-key get and set loop.
requirements.statusDetail: Fixed: closes FUNC-71. Every read verb was strictly one key or map at a time and list endpoints returned metadata or names only, never values; Fafnir's backend already had a bulk-value endpoint but it existed solely for gimle-agent's internal fetch and no CLI verb wrapped it. SecretStore.getMany now serves a whole batch from one store listing, exposed as GET /secrets/{tenantId}?names=a,b,c behind a dedicated authorizeSecretsBulkRead, and the CLI gained export and import. The security posture was treated as the deliverable rather than the test count: the bulk read runs Fafnir's own independent Authorizer.authorize check, is deliberately not routed through the node self-service short-circuit and refuses any gimle:nodes principal outright so the path never widens a node identity's reach, and both allow and deny are audited. A key that is unknown or soft-deleted is omitted rather than failing the whole batch. At-rest posture, deliberate and documented: the export file holds plaintext material, base64-encoded but not encrypted, because ciphertext under the source cluster's master key is useless at a destination with a different one -- which is the whole reason the command exists. Compensating constraints: the destination must be a file, never stdout; it is created rw------- where POSIX permissions exist; an existing path is refused rather than overwritten; and deleting the file after import is stated as the operator's responsibility in both the CLI output and the docs.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: SecretStoreTest (2); FafnirServerTest (2); FafnirSecretsAuthzTest (the bulk read runs its own authorizer check and forbids an ungranted caller; is allowed for a caller holding SECRET read; a node is forbidden the bulk read even with an active assignment while keeping its single-key read); SecretCommandTest (5, including owner-only file mode, refusal to overwrite, and a soft-deleted secret omitted).
gherkinSteps: Given a tenant with several live secrets
When they are exported and imported into another tenant
Then every value and declared type round-trips
And a node identity is refused the bulk read while keeping its single-key read

requirements.feature: Secret and config payloads are bounded on both the value and the raw request body
requirements.userStory: As an operator, I want an oversized secret or config write refused with a clear error, so that a multi-megabyte blob is not silently accepted, encrypted and replicated through Raft consensus.
requirements.statusDetail: Fixed: closes FUNC-72. Neither a secret's plaintext nor a config value's byte length was checked anywhere in the write path, and the HTTP body itself was read unbounded via readAllBytes() with no Content-Length cap in both FafnirServer and ApiServer; the only nearby admission guardrails check CPU, memory and instance counts, never payload size. Limits are now enforced at both layers: ConfigEntry.MAX_VALUE_BYTES is 1 MiB (the storage row ceiling, matching Kubernetes' own Secret/ConfigMap limit), SecretStore.MAX_VALUE_BYTES and ApiServer.MAX_CONFIG_VALUE_BYTES are 512 KiB (half of it, so a value accepted at write time still fits once encrypted), and request bodies are capped at 4 MiB in both servers using the existing com.gimle.core.io.SizeLimitedInputStream on the streamed bytes rather than trusting Content-Length -- so an oversized body is refused before it is buffered whole.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: ApiServerPayloadLimitTest (new), SecretStoreTest and FafnirServerTest boundary cases on both the value-length and request-body paths.
gherkinSteps: Given a secret value larger than the configured ceiling
When it is written
Then the write is refused with a clear error
And the oversized request body is rejected before being buffered whole

requirements.feature: Logs can be filtered by level threshold and text at the reader, on every surface
requirements.userStory: As an operator hunting one ERROR line during an incident, I want to filter logs by level and text on both the CLI and the console, so that I am not paging through raw unfiltered NDJSON by hand.
requirements.statusDetail: Fixed: closes FUNC-38. LogFileReader, the shared primitive behind every log route, filtered only by timestamp cursor -- no level or text parameter existed anywhere in its signature -- so the CLI accepted only --category/--follow/--since and the console coloured a line by level after the fact but never filtered by it. A new LogFilter record in gimle-core carries both predicates and is taken by every log reader, so both surfaces get filtering from one mechanism rather than two implementations. Level is a threshold (TRACE < DEBUG < INFO < WARN < ERROR); a line with no level, or one off that scale such as a raw SYSTEM capture, cannot be ranked and is excluded rather than silently admitted, and an unrecognized level is a 400 naming the accepted values. Text is plain case-insensitive substring, deliberately not regex, matched against message/logger/stackTrace/raw only and never nodeId/thread where a short query would match every line from one node. Filtering happens server-side at the reader so a high-volume log is not shipped in full; the filter is applied before limit, so a page is the last N matching lines; and streamFollow suppresses non-matching lines while still advancing its cursor past them so a quiet run is not re-scanned every tick. The parameters thread through AgentLogServer, the ApiServer /logs/* proxy and the Muninn fallback identically, so an operator gets the same result whether or not the owning node is still alive. A zero-match query is legible on every surface rather than silent.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: LogFilterTest (18), LogFileReaderFilteringTest (8), AgentLogServerTest (7 new), MuninnDayFileStoreTest, MuninnLogFilterParityTest (6 -- asserts the Muninn fallback returns exactly what the live-agent reader returns for the same lines and filter), ApiServerLogsFallbackTest (7 new), LogsCommandTest (7), and 43 console Vitest cases across lib, route, Mock and Http repository tests.
gherkinSteps: Given a log containing lines at several levels
When it is read with a level threshold of WARN and a text filter
Then only matching WARN and ERROR lines are returned
And the same query against a gone node's shipped history returns the same lines
And a query matching nothing reports that rather than returning silence

requirements.feature: A deleted config or secret key is retracted from a running instance, and modules can subscribe to changes
requirements.userStory: As an operator revoking a credential, I want deleting a key to take effect on already-running instances, so that a stale value does not stay live and readable until the instance happens to restart.
requirements.statusDetail: Fixed: closes FUNC-39. Config and secret hot-reload was real and push-based, but ConfigRelay relayed only creates and updates -- its own comment confirmed a key deleted upstream was deliberately never retracted from a running instance -- so deleting a key to revoke it had no effect until restart, leaving the stale value live and readable indefinitely. Separately ModuleContext exposed only pull-based config(key)/configKeys(), documented as a snapshot rather than a live view, with no listener a module could register, so a module wanting to react to a rotated credential had only its own polling. Retraction is now real and level-triggered: the relay delivers the authoritative current key set (ControlMessage.ConfigKeysRetained) so an instance converges from any starting state rather than depending on a delete event it might have missed, and a hosted module may register a listener called on every delivery, rotation and retraction of a key it can see. The javadoc and comments that documented non-retraction and the snapshot-only view as deliberate choices were rewritten, since leaving them would make the code lie about itself.
requirements.testCoverageDetail: ModuleConfigRetractionTest (new, including convergence from an arbitrary starting state rather than only a clean delete event), ConfigRelayTest, ControlMessageCodecTest.
gherkinSteps: Given a running instance holding a config key
When that key is deleted upstream
Then the instance stops being able to read it without restarting
And a module listener is notified of the retraction

requirements.feature: Trace sampling is configurable and parent-based
requirements.userStory: As an operator running a high-throughput workload, I want to dial trace volume down without a code change, so that one full span per fabric call on every hop is not the only option.
requirements.statusDetail: Fixed: closes FUNC-59. Every SdkTracerProvider was built with no setSampler call, so the OTel SDK default of Sampler.alwaysOn() applied; no sampler configuration existed anywhere in the codebase and, unlike other deliberate defaults here, 100% sampling was never called out as an intentional choice in the observability docs. The recorded fraction is now configurable per process via -Dgimle.tracing.samplingRatio (0.0-1.0, default 1.0, so existing behavior is unchanged unless an operator opts in), honoured identically by every tracer-provider install path.
